## Approved Plan:
# Implement color components (tasks #297, #298, #299)

## Context

GitHub issues #297, #298, #299 (epic #227 "Agnostic specialized components") ask for
the framework-agnostic core of eight color components plus the shared `ColorValue`
foundation they all depend on. No adapter (Leptos/Dioxus) work is in scope.

- **#297 (3 pts):** shared `ColorValue` type + helpers, `ColorSwatch` (stateless), `ColorField` (stateful Idle/Focused).
- **#298 (5 pts):** `ColorArea` (stateful 2D), `ColorSlider` (stateful 1D). Both Idle/Dragging, shared pointer-drag pattern.
- **#299 (5 pts):** `ColorWheel` + `AngleSlider` (circular drag), `ColorSwatchPicker` (listbox of swatches).

The shared color types are the real dependency that ties the three issues together
(the issues say "Depends on: None" only because there is no separate ColorValue issue;
#297's goal explicitly introduces it). The spec authoritatively defines `ColorValue`,
`ColorChannel`, `ColorFormat`, `ColorSpace`, `ColorNameParts`, and the color
math/parse/format helpers in `spec/components/specialized/color-picker.md` §Types
(L28-568), and `_category.md` states all color logic lives in `ars-core`.

### User decisions (this session)
1. **Delivery: one combined PR** closing all three issues (`Closes #297`, `Closes #298`, `Closes #299`).
2. **Shared types live in a flat `crates/ars-core/src/color.rs`** module (`ars_core::color::*`).
   This requires renaming the `color_picker` module name to `color` in the color specs' import lines.

## Architecture / layout

### ars-core: the shared color foundation (`crates/ars-core/src/color.rs`)
New flat module, declared `pub mod color;` in `crates/ars-core/src/lib.rs`, with the
key value types re-exported at the crate root alongside `Direction`/`Orientation`
(`pub use color::{ColorValue, ColorChannel, ColorFormat, ColorSpace, ColorNameParts};`).
Port verbatim from color-picker.md §Types:
- `ColorValue { hue, saturation, lightness, alpha }` (HSL+alpha storage) with
  `new`, `from_hsl`, `to_rgb`, `to_rgba`, `to_hex`, `to_css_hsl`, `to_hsb`, `from_rgb`,
  `from_hex`, `Default` (pure red). Bodies are given in the spec (L52-192) — copy exactly.
- WCAG helpers: `relative_luminance`, `contrast_ratio`, `passes_wcag_aa`, `passes_wcag_aaa` (L200-235).
- `ColorNameParts { lightness, chroma, hue }` (all `String`) + perceptual naming:
  `color_name_parts(&self) -> ColorNameParts` (NO args, returns English keys) and
  `color_name_en(&self) -> String`. Implement the OKLCH classification described in the
  doc comment (L271-284): HSL→sRGB→OKLab→OKLCH, 5 lightness buckets, 3 chroma buckets,
  13 hue buckets, gray/white/black special-case. (Björn Ottosson OKLab math — well defined.)
- Enums: `ColorFormat` (Hex/Rgb/Hsl/Hsb), `ColorSpace` (Rgb/Hsl/Hsb/Hwb), `ColorChannel`
  (Hue/Saturation/Lightness/Brightness/Alpha/Red/Green/Blue), `DragTarget`.
- Free fns: `channel_value`, `with_channel`, `channel_range`, `channel_step_default`,
  `parse_color_string`, `format_color_string` (+ private `strip_fn_call`, `parse_rgb_args`,
  `parse_hsl_args`, `parse_hsb_args`). Bodies given in spec (L388-548) — copy exactly.

`#![no_std]` constraints: ars-core is `no_std`-compatible; use `alloc` (`String`, `format!`,
`Vec`) like `badge.rs` does, and `libm`/`f64` methods available in core where needed
(`powf`, `atan2`, `cbrt` for OKLab — confirm availability; ars-core already uses float math).

### ars-components: eight component modules under `src/specialized/`
Each follows the **slider** reference pattern (`crates/ars-components/src/input/slider/mod.rs`)
for stateful drag machines and the **badge** pattern (`src/data_display/badge.rs`) for the
stateless swatch. Register each in `crates/ars-components/src/specialized/mod.rs`.

Directory-backed modules (`mod.rs` + `snapshots/`) per the repo's mod.rs convention:
- `specialized/color_swatch/mod.rs` — **stateless**. `Api::new(props, env, messages)`, Parts
  `Root`/`Inner`, Messages `format_name`/`role_description`. Mirror `badge.rs` for the
  no-machine `Api` + empty-id handling (resolve the spec's `generate_id()` to badge's actual id strategy).
- `specialized/color_field/mod.rs` — **stateful** Idle/Focused. `type Effect = NoEffect`.
  Machine bodies (`format_value`, `commit_input`, `adjust_channel`, `init`, `transition`)
  are fully given in color-field.md §1.5 (L184-503). Parts: Root/Label/Input/Description/
  ErrorMessage/HiddenInput. Whole-color vs channel (spinbutton) modes; IME suppression.
- `specialized/color_area/mod.rs` — **stateful** Idle/Dragging, 2D. Parts Root/Background/
  Thumb/HiddenInput. `Effect` enum (`ValueChangeEnd`) for `on_change_end`. `apply_area_position`
  maps normalized (x,y)→two channels (y inverted). Adapter supplies normalized coords.
- `specialized/color_slider/mod.rs` — **stateful** Idle/Dragging, 1D. Parts Root/Label/Track/
  Thumb/Output/HiddenInput. Orientation + RTL keyboard. `apply_slider_position`. `Effect` enum.
- `specialized/color_wheel/mod.rs` — **stateful** Idle/Dragging, circular hue. Parts Root/Track/
  Thumb/HiddenInput. No `aria-orientation`, no RTL flip. `apply_wheel_angle`. `Effect` enum.
- `specialized/angle_slider/mod.rs` — **stateful** Idle/Dragging/Focused, `Bindable<f64>` (NOT
  ColorValue), custom min/max. Parts Root/Control/Track/Range/Thumb/ValueText/MarkerGroup/
  Marker{value}/HiddenInput. `compute_angle`/`snap_to_step`/`wrap_value` helpers. `Effect` enum.
- `specialized/color_swatch_picker/mod.rs` — **stateful** Idle/Focused listbox. Parts Root/
  Item{index}/HiddenInput. `colors: Vec<ColorValue>`, `focused_index`, grid/stack layout,
  roving tabindex, `item_swatch_props(index) -> color_swatch::Props` embedding ColorSwatch.

All import shared types from `ars_core::color::{...}`. Stateful machines use `Bindable`,
`TransitionPlan`, `ComponentIds`, `AttrMap`, `ConnectApi` from `ars_core` exactly as slider does.

## Spec reconciliation (same PR — CLAUDE.md mandates resolving drift)

These are corrections to existing drift, not feature changes (issues say "no spec change required");
each is required to make the spec compile against reality:
1. **Module rename** `color_picker` → `color` in import lines of all color specs
   (`color-swatch.md`, `color-field.md`, `color-area.md`, `color-slider.md`, `color-wheel.md`,
   `color-swatch-picker.md`, and the defining `color-picker.md` path comment at L34).
2. **Import path drift**: `use crate::machine::{Machine, TransitionPlan, ComponentIds, AttrMap}`
   does not exist — reconcile spec code blocks to real ars-core paths (`ars_core::{AttrMap,
   ComponentIds, Machine, TransitionPlan, ...}`).
3. **`color_name_parts` arity**: color-swatch.md (the in-scope consumer) uses the no-arg
   English-keys form; color-picker.md §Color Name Parts uses `(locale, messages)`. Resolve to
   the no-arg form (localization happens at the component `Messages::format_name` layer) and
   update color-picker.md §Color Name Parts to match.
4. **`type Effect`**: color-field.md §1.5 omits the required `type Effect` — add `= NoEffect`.
   Verify area/slider/wheel/angle declare a bespoke `Effect` enum for `on_change_end`.
5. **`generate_id()`** in color-swatch.md — reconcile to badge's actual empty-id strategy.

Use `cargo xtask spec validate` after edits.

## Testing strategy (TDD — tests first per named tests in each issue)

- **ars-core unit tests** in `color.rs` `#[cfg(test)]`: parse hex/rgb/hsl/hsb, format round-trips,
  channel range/value/with_channel, WCAG ratios, `color_name_en` for known colors (red/white/
  black/blue), HSL↔RGB↔HSB conversions. Add a proptest (ars-core already deps proptest) for
  conversion round-trip stability and clamp invariants.
- **Component unit + snapshot tests** inline in each `mod.rs` (`Service::<Machine>::new` for
  stateful, `Api::new` for swatch), `insta` `.snap` fixtures in each `snapshots/` dir. Cover
  every Part's `*_attrs()` and each output-affecting state/prop/context branch (the issues'
  "Tests to add first" lists are the checklist). Run `cargo insta test --unreferenced=reject`.
- **Spec-conformance**: extend `crates/ars-components/tests/spec_conformance/specialized.rs`
  with `assert_anatomy("<scope>", &[(Part::X, "x"), ...])` for all 8 components.
- **Proptest state machines**: add `crates/ars-components/tests/proptest_state_machines/
  specialized.rs` and route `mod specialized;` in `proptest_state_machines.rs`, using
  `common::proptest_config()`; assert state-transition invariants for the stateful machines.
- Document all public items (`missing_docs`), zero warnings, `#[expect(...)]` not `#[allow]`.

## Critical reference files
- `crates/ars-components/src/input/slider/mod.rs` — drag-machine pattern (State/Event/Context/
  Props/Effect/Machine/Part/Api, `value_from_pointer`, `on_thumb_keydown`, snapshot tests).
- `crates/ars-components/src/data_display/badge.rs` — stateless `Api::new` pattern for swatch.
- `crates/ars-core/src/lib.rs` — `Machine` trait, `Bindable`, `Env`, `NoEffect`, `Service`, root re-exports.
- `crates/ars-components/tests/spec_conformance/specialized.rs` + `helper.rs` — anatomy assertions.
- `spec/components/specialized/color-picker.md` §Types (L28-568) — verbatim ColorValue source.
- `spec/components/specialized/color-field.md` §1.5 (L184-503) — verbatim field machine.

## Verification
1. `cargo test -p ars-core color` — shared types pass.
2. `cargo insta test -p ars-components --unreferenced=reject` — review/accept new `.snap` fixtures.
3. `cargo test -p ars-components` — unit/snapshot/spec-conformance/proptest green.
4. `cargo xtask spec validate` — spec frontmatter/manifest consistency after reconciliation edits.
5. Run the **`post-implementation-audit`** skill (mandatory) — land every finding in this PR.
6. Present to user for review; on approval run `cargo xci-fast` and fix failures.

  "content": "//! Shared color value types and helpers for the color components.\n//!\n//! The internal color representation is [`ColorValue`] (HSL + alpha). All other\n//! color spaces (RGB, HEX, HSB/HSV, CSS) are computed on demand via conversion\n//! methods. These types are the value layer shared by every color component\n//! (`ColorSwatch`, `ColorField`, `ColorArea`, `ColorSlider`, `ColorWheel`,\n//! `ColorSwatchPicker`, and the future `ColorPicker`); `AngleSlider` is the one\n//! exception — it operates on bare `f64` degrees.\n//!\n//! Live geometry (track/area measurement, pointer capture,\n//! coordinate-to-value conversion) is supplied by adapters via native handles;\n//! this module only owns the channel math, parsing, formatting, perceptual\n//! naming, and WCAG contrast utilities.\n\nuse alloc::{\n    format,\n    string::{String, ToString},\n    vec::Vec,\n};\n\nuse core_maths::CoreFloat;\n\n/// A color value stored in HSL with alpha. All other formats are computed.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub struct ColorValue {\n    /// Hue in degrees [0, 360).\n    pub hue: f64,\n    /// Saturation as a fraction [0.0, 1.0].\n `ColorValue` from the given hue, saturation, lightness, and alpha.\n    ///\n    /// Hue is wrapped into `[0, 360)`; saturation, lightness, and alpha are\n    /// clamped to `[0.0, 1.0]`.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn new(hue: f64, saturation: f64, lightness: f64, alpha: f64) -> Self {\n        debug_assert!(hue.is_finite(), \"hue must be finite\");\n        debug_assert!(saturation.is_finite(), \"saturation must be finite\");\n        debug_assert!(lightness.is_finite(), \"lightness must be finite\");\n        debug_assert!(alpha.is_finite(), \"alpha must be finite\");\n        Self {\n            hue: hue.rem_euclid(360.0),\n            saturation: saturation.clamp(0.0, 1.0),\n            lightness: lightness.clamp(0.0, 1.0),\n            alpha: alpha.clamp(0.0, 1.0),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create from an HSL triplet with full alpha.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn from_hsl(h: f64, s: f64, l: f64) -> Self {\n        Self::new(h, s, l, 1.0)\n    }\n\n    /// Convert to RGB (0-255 per channel).\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn to_rgb(&self) -> (u8, u8, u8) {\n        let h = self.hue / 360.0;\n        let s = self.saturation;\n        let l = self.lightness;\n        let c = (1.0 - (2.0 * l - 1.0).abs()) * s;\n        let x = c * (1.0 - ((h * 6.0) % 2.0 - 1.0).abs());\n        let m = l - c / 2.0;\n        let (r1, g1, b1) = match (h * 6.0).floor() as u8 {\n            0 => (c, x, 0.0),\n            1 => (x, c, 0.0),\n            2 => (0.0, c, x),\n            3 => (0.0, x, c),\n            4 => (x, 0.0, c),\n            _ => (c, 0.0, x),\n        };\n        (\n            ((r1 + m) * 255.0).round() as u8,\n            ((g1 + m) * 255.0).round() as u8,\n            ((b1 + m) * 255.0).round() as u8,\n        )\n    }\n\n 255.0).round() as u8)\n    }\n\n    /// Convert to hex string (6-digit or 8-digit with alpha).\n    ///\n    /// The alpha component is only emitted when `include_alpha` is set *and*\n    /// the color is not fully opaque.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn to_hex(&self, include_alpha: bool) -> String {\n        let (r, g, b) = self.to_rgb();\n        if include_alpha && self.alpha < 1.0 {\n   format!(\n                \"hsl({:.0}, {:.1}%, {:.1}%)\",\n                self.hue,\n                self.saturation * 100.0,\n                self.lightness * 100.0,\n            )\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Convert to HSB/HSV representation `(hue, saturation, brightness)`.\n    ///\n    /// Hue is shared with the HSL representation; saturation and brightness are\n    /// the HSB-space components in `[0.0, 1.0]`.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn to_hsb(&self) -> (f64, f64, f64) {\n        let l = self.lightness;\n        let s = self.saturation;\n        let v = l + s * l.min(1.0 - l);\n        let sv = if v == 0.0 { 0.0 } else { 2.0 * (1.0 - l / v) };\n        (self.hue, sv, v)\n    }\n\n    /// Create from RGB values (0-255).\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn from_rgb(r: u8, g: u8, b: u8) -> Self {\n        let r = f64::from(r) / 255.0;\n        let g = f64::from(g) / 255.0;\n        let b = f64::from(b) / 255.0;\n        let max = r.max(g).max(b);\n        let min = r.min(g).min(b);\n        let l = (max + min) / 2.0;\n        if max == min {\n            return Self::new(0.0, 0.0, l, 1.0);\n        }\n        let d = max - min;\n        let s = if l > 0.5 {\n            d / (2.0 - max - min)\n        } else {\n            d / (max + min)\n        };\n        let h = if max == r {\n            ((g - b) / d + if g < b { 6.0 } else { 0.0 }) * 60.0\n        } else if max == g {\n            ((b - r) / d + 2.0) * 60.0\n        } else {\n            ((r - g) / d + 4.0) * 60.0\n        };\n        Self::new(h, s, l, 1.0)\n    }\n\n    /// Parse a hex string (`#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`).\n    ///\n    /// Returns `None` for any string whose hex digit count is neither 6 nor 8\n    /// or that contains non-hex characters.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn from_hex(hex: &str) -> Option<Self> {\n        let hex = hex.trim_start_matches('#');\n        match hex.len() {\n            6 => {\n                let r = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[0..2], 16).ok()?;\n                let g = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[2..4], 16).ok()?;\n                let b = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[4..6], 16).ok()?;\n                Some(Self::from_rgb(r, g, b))\n            }\n            8 => {\n                let r = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[0..2], 16).ok()?;\n                let g = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[2..4], 16).ok()?;\n                let b = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[4..6], 16).ok()?;\n                let a = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[6..8], 16).ok()?;\n                let mut color = Self::from_rgb(r, g, b);\n                color.alpha = f64::from(a) / 255.0;\n                Some(color)\n            }\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for ColorValue {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new(0.0, 1.0, 0.5, 1.0) // Pure red, full opacity\n    }\n}\n\n// ── WCAG contrast utilities ─────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Linearize a single sRGB channel (0-255) per the WCAG 2.1 sRGB definition.\nfn srgb_to_linear(c: u8) -> f64 {\n    let c = f64::from(c) / 255.0;\n    if c <= 0.040_45 {\n        c / 12.92\n    } else {\n        ((c + 0.055) / 1.055).powf(2.4)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl ColorValue {\n    /// Compute the relative luminance per the WCAG 2.1 definition.\n    ///\n    /// Uses the sRGB linearization formula: if `C <= 0.04045`, `C / 12.92`;\n    /// else `((C + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4`. Returns a value in `[0.0, 1.0]`.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn relative_luminance(&self) -> f64 {\n        let (r, g, b) = self.to_rgb();\n        0.2126 * srgb_to_linear(r) + 0.7152 * srgb_to_linear(g) + 0.0722 * srgb_to_linear(b)\n    }\n\n    /// Compute the WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio between two colors.\n    ///\n    /// Returns a value in `[1.0, 21.0]`. Higher is more contrast.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn contrast_ratio(&self, other: &ColorValue) -> f64 {\n        let l1 = self.relative_luminance();\n        let l2 = other.relative_luminance();\n        let (lighter, darker) = if l1 > l2 { (l1, l2) } else { (l2, l1) };\n        (lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05)\n    }\n\n    /// Check if this color passes WCAG AA contrast against another color.\n    ///\n    /// Normal text: 4.5:1; large text (>= 18pt or >= 14pt bold): 3:1.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn passes_wcag_aa(&self, other: &ColorValue, large_text: bool) -> bool {\n        let ratio = self.contrast_ratio(other);\n        if large_text { ratio >= 3.0 } else { ratio >= 4.5 }\n    }\n\n    /// Check if this color passes WCAG AAA contrast against another color.\n    ///\n    /// Normal text: 7:1; large text: 4.5:1.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn passes_wcag_aaa(&self, other: &ColorValue, large_text: bool) -> bool {\n        let ratio = self.contrast_ratio(other);\n        if large_text { ratio >= 4.5 } else { ratio >= 7.0 }\n    }\n}\n\n// ── Perceptual color naming ─────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Describes a color in human-readable terms for screen readers.\n///\n/// Components: lightness modifier, chroma modifier, and hue name. Parts are\n/// returned as `String` (not `&'static str`) so the i18n layer can substitute\n/// localized labels. [`ColorValue::color_name_parts`] returns English keys; a\n/// component's `format_name` message maps and orders them per locale.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ColorNameParts {\n    /// e.g., \"dark\", \"light\", \"very dark\", \"very light\", or \"\" for medium.\n    pub lightness: String,\n    /// e.g., \"vibrant\", \"pale\", or \"\" for moderate.\n    pub chroma: String,\n    /// e.g., \"red\", \"blue\", \"cyan-blue\", \"gray\", \"white\", \"black\".\n    pub hue: String,\n}\n\n/// Map an OKLCH hue angle (degrees, 0-360) to one of 13 named hue buckets.\nfn hue_name(h: f64) -> &'static str {\n    match h {\n        x if x < 35.0 => \"red\",\n        x if x < 55.0 => \"red-orange\",\n        x if x < 75.0 => \"orange\",\n        x if x < 90.0 => \"yellow-orange\",\n        x if x < 110.0 => \"yellow\",\n        x if x < 135.0 => \"yellow-green\",\n        x if x < 165.0 => \"green\",\n        x if x < 185.0 => \"cyan-green\",\n        x if x < 205.0 => \"cyan\",\n        x if x < 240.0 => \"cyan-blue\",\n        x if x < 280.0 => \"blue\",\n        x if x < 320.0 => \"purple\",\n        x if x < 350.0 => \"magenta\",\n        _ => \"red\",\n    }\n}\n\nimpl ColorValue {\n    /// Convert this color to OKLCH `(lightness, chroma, hue_degrees)`.\n    ///\n    /// OKLCH is a perceptually uniform space; classifying in it yields more\n    /// natural color names than classifying in HSL. Uses Björn Ottosson's\n    /// OKLab transform from linear sRGB.\n    fn to_oklch(&self) -> (f64, f64, f64) {\n        let (r, g, b) = self.to_rgb();\n        let lr = srgb_to_linear(r);\n        let lg = srgb_to_linear(g);\n        let lb = srgb_to_linear(b);\n\n        let l = 0.412_221_470_8 * lr + 0.536_332_536_3 * lg + 0.051_445_992_9 * lb;\n        let m = 0.211_903_498_2 * lr + 0.680_699_545_1 * lg + 0.107_396_956_6 * lb;\n        let s = 0.088_302_461_9 * lr + 0.281_718_837_6 * lg + 0.629_978_700_5 * lb;\n\n        let l_ = l.cbrt();\n        let m_ = m.cbrt();\n        let s_ = s.cbrt();\n\n        let big_l = 0.210_454_255_3 * l_ + 0.793_617_785_0 * m_ - 0.004_072_046_8 * s_;\n        let a = 1.977_998_495_1 * l_ - 2.428_592_205_0 * m_ + 0.450_593_709_9 * s_;\n        let bb = 0.025_904_037_1 * l_ + 0.782_771_766_2 * m_ - 0.808_675_766_0 * s_;\n\n        let chroma = (a * a + bb * bb).sqrt();\n        // atan2 returns radians in (-PI, PI]; convert to degrees and wrap to [0, 360).\n        let hue = (bb.atan2(a) * (180.0 / core::f64::consts::PI)).rem_euclid(360.0);\n        (big_l, chroma, hue)\n    }\n\n    /// Returns English color description parts for accessibility.\n    ///\n    /// The parts (lightness modifier, chroma modifier, hue name) are English\n    /// keys; the localized, reordered string is produced by a component's\n    /// `format_name` message. Classification runs in OKLCH:\n    ///\n    /// 1. Lightness → 5 levels: very dark (`<0.2`), dark (`<0.4`), medium/`\"\"`\n    ///    (`<0.6`), light (`<0.8`), very light (`>=0.8`).\n    /// 2. Chroma → grayish (`<0.04`), moderate/`\"\"` (`<0.12`), vibrant\n    ///    (`>=0.12`); moderate chroma with light lightness reads as \"pale\".\n    /// 3. Near-zero chroma collapses to \"black\"/\"gray\"/\"white\" by lightness.\n    /// 4. Hue angle → one of 13 named buckets (see [`hue_name`]).\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn color_name_parts(&self) -> ColorNameParts {\n        let (l, c, h) = self.to_oklch();\n\n        // Near-gray: chroma is too low for a meaningful hue name.\n        if c < 0.04 {\n            let achromatic = if l < 0.2 {\n                \"black\"\n            } else if l > 0.85 {\n                \"white\"\n            } else {\n                \"gray\"\n            };\n            return ColorNameParts {\n                lightness: String::new(),\n                chroma: String::new(),\n                hue: achromatic.to_string(),\n            };\n        }\n\n        let lightness = if l < 0.2 {\n            \"very dark\"\n        } else if l < 0.4 {\n            \"dark\"\n        } else if l < 0.6 {\n            \"\"\n        } else if l < 0.8 {\n            \"light\"\n        } else {\n            \"very light\"\n        };\n\n        let chroma = if c > 0.12 {\n            \"vibrant\"\n        } else if l > 0.7 {\n            \"pale\"\n        } else {\n            \"\"\n        };\n\n        ColorNameParts {\n            lightness: lightness.to_string(),\n            chroma: chroma.to_string(),\n            hue: hue_name(h).to_string(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Convenience: format as an English-order string such as \"dark vibrant blue\".\n    ///\n    /// Joins the non-empty [`ColorNameParts`] with single spaces. Intended for\n    /// tests and non-localized contexts; localized callers use a component's\n    /// `format_name` message instead.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn color_name_en(&self) -> String {\n        let parts = self.color_name_parts();\n        [\n            parts.lightness.as_str(),\n            parts.chroma.as_str(),\n            parts.hue.as_str(),\n        ]\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())\n        .copied()\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n        .join(\" \")\n    }\n}\n\n// ── Supporting enums ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The color format currently displayed in a text input area.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]\npub enum ColorFormat {\n    /// The `#rrggbb` / `#rrggbbaa` hex format.\n    #[default]\n    Hex,\n    /// The `rgb()` / `rgba()` format.\n    Rgb,\n    /// The `hsl()` / `hsla()` format.\n    Hsl,\n    /// The `hsb()` format.\n    Hsb,\n}\n\n/// Color space for the picker controls.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]\npub enum ColorSpace {\n    /// The RGB color space.\n    Rgb,\n    /// The HSL color space.\n    #[default]\n    Hsl,\n    /// The HSB color space.\n    Hsb,\n    /// The HWB color space.\n    Hwb,\n}\n\n/// Individual color channel identifier, used by `ColorArea`, `ColorSlider`,\n/// `ColorField`, and `ColorPicker` for per-channel operations.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]\npub enum ColorChannel {\n    /// The hue channel (0-360 degrees).\n    #[default]\n    Hue,\n    /// The saturation channel (0.0-1.0).\n    Saturation,\n    /// The lightness channel (0.0-1.0).\n    Lightness,\n    /// The brightness channel (HSB/HSV value component, 0.0-1.0).\n    Brightness,\n    /// The alpha channel (0.0-1.0).\n    Alpha,\n    /// The red channel (0-255).\n    Red,\n    /// The green channel (0-255).\n    Green,\n    /// The blue channel (0-255).\n    Blue,\n}\n\n/// Identifies what the user is dragging in the `ColorPicker`.\n///\n/// The `ColorPicker` area targets two channels at once, while channel sliders\n/// target a single channel.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DragTarget {\n    /// 2D area: `x_channel = Saturation`, `y_channel = Lightness` (fixed in `ColorPicker`).\n    Area,\n    /// 1D channel slider.\n    Channel(ColorChannel),\n}\n\n// ── Channel helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Get the current value of a single channel from a [`ColorValue`].\n#[must_use]\npub fn channel_value(color: &ColorValue, channel: ColorChannel) -> f64 {\n    match channel {\n        ColorChannel::Hue => color.hue,\n        ColorChannel::Saturation => color.saturation,\n        ColorChannel::Lightness => color.lightness,\n        ColorChannel::Brightness => color.to_hsb().2,\n        ColorChannel::Alpha => color.alpha,\n        ColorChannel::Red => f64::from(color.to_rgb().0),\n        ColorChannel::Green => f64::from(color.to_rgb().1),\n        ColorChannel::Blue => f64::from(color.to_rgb().2),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Return a new [`ColorValue`] with one channel replaced.\n#[must_use]\npub fn with_channel(color: &ColorValue, channel: ColorChannel, value: f64) -> ColorValue {\n    match channel {\n        ColorChannel::Hue => ColorValue::new(value, color.saturation, color.lightness, color.alpha),\n        ColorChannel::Saturation => {\n            ColorValue::new(color.hue, value, color.lightness, color.alpha)\n        }\n        ColorChannel::Lightness => {\n            ColorValue::new(color.hue, color.saturation, value, color.alpha)\n        }\n        ColorChannel::Brightness => {\n            // Convert current HSL to HSB, replace B, convert back.\n            let (h, s_hsb, _) = color.to_hsb();\n            let v = value.clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n            let l = v * (1.0 - s_hsb / 2.0);\n            let s_hsl = if l == 0.0 || l == 1.0 {\n                0.0\n            } else {\n                (v - l) / l.min(1.0 - l)\n            };\n            ColorValue::new(h, s_hsl, l, color.alpha)\n        }\n        ColorChannel::Alpha => {\n            ColorValue::new(color.hue, color.saturation, color.lightness, value)\n        }\n        ColorChannel::Red => {\n            let (_, g, b) = color.to_rgb();\n            let mut c = ColorValue::from_rgb(value.round() as u8, g, b);\n            c.alpha = color.alpha;\n            c\n        }\n        ColorChannel::Green => {\n            let (r, _, b) = color.to_rgb();\n            let mut c = ColorValue::from_rgb(r, value.round() as u8, b);\n            c.alpha = color.alpha;\n            c\n        }\n        ColorChannel::Blue => {\n            let (r, g, _) = color.to_rgb();\n            let mut c = ColorValue::from_rgb(r, g, value.round() as u8);\n            c.alpha = color.alpha;\n            c\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// The `(min, max)` range for a channel.\n#[must_use]\npub fn channel_range(channel: ColorChannel) -> (f64, f64) {\n    match channel {\n        ColorChannel::Hue => (0.0, 360.0),\n        ColorChannel::Red | ColorChannel::Green | ColorChannel::Blue => (0.0, 255.0),\n        // Saturation, Lightness, Brightness, Alpha\n        _ => (0.0, 1.0),\n    }\n}\n\n/// The default step size for keyboard adjustment of a channel.\n#[must_use]\npub fn channel_step_default(channel: ColorChannel) -> f64 {\n    match channel {\n        // 1 degree for hue, 1 unit for the 0-255 RGB channels.\n        ColorChannel::Hue\n        | ColorChannel::Red\n        | ColorChannel::Green\n        | ColorChannel::Blue => 1.0,\n        // 1% for the 0..1 range channels.\n        _ => 0.01,\n    }\n}\n\n// ── String parsing / formatting ─────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Strip a functional notation call: `name(...)` -> inner content.\nfn strip_fn_call<'a>(input: &'a str, name: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {\n    let stripped = input.strip_prefix(name)?;\n    let stripped = stripped.strip_prefix('(')?.strip_suffix(')')?;\n    Some(stripped)\n}\n\n/// Parse `r, g, b` or `r, g, b, a` inside `rgb()` / `rgba()`.\nfn parse_rgb_args(inner: &str, has_alpha: bool) -> Option<ColorValue> {\n    let parts: Vec<&str> = inner.split(',').map(str::trim).collect();\n    if has_alpha && parts.len() != 4 {\n        return None;\n    }\n    if !has_alpha && parts.len() != 3 {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let r: u8 = parts[0].parse().ok()?;\n    let g: u8 = parts[1].parse().ok()?;\n    let b: u8 = parts[2].parse().ok()?;\n    let a: f64 = if has_alpha { parts[3].parse().ok()? } else { 1.0 };\n\n    let mut c = ColorValue::from_rgb(r, g, b);\n    c.alpha = a.clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n    Some(c)\n}\n\n/// Parse `h, s%, l%` or `h, s%, l%, a` inside `hsl()` / `hsla()`.\nfn parse_hsl_args(inner: &str, has_alpha: bool) -> Option<ColorValue> {\n    let parts: Vec<&str> = inner.split(',').map(str::trim).collect();\n    if has_alpha && parts.len() != 4 {\n        return None;\n    }\n    if !has_alpha && parts.len() != 3 {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let h: f64 = parts[0].parse().ok()?;\n    let s: f64 = parts[1].strip_suffix('%')?.trim().parse::<f64>().ok()? / 100.0;\n    let l: f64 = parts[2].strip_suffix('%')?.trim().parse::<f64>().ok()? / 100.0;\n    let a: f64 = if has_alpha { parts[3].parse().ok()? } else { 1.0 };\n\n    Some(ColorValue::new(h, s, l, a.clamp(0.0, 1.0)))\n}\n\n/// Parse `h, s%, b%` inside `hsb()`.\nfn parse_hsb_args(inner: &str) -> Option<ColorValue> {\n    let parts: Vec<&str> = inner.split(',').map(str::trim).collect();\n    if parts.len() != 3 {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let h: f64 = parts[0].parse().ok()?;\n    let s: f64 = parts[1].strip_suffix('%')?.trim().parse::<f64>().ok()? / 100.0;\n    let b: f64 = parts[2].strip_suffix('%')?.trim().parse::<f64>().ok()? / 100.0;\n    // Convert HSB -> HSL: lightness = b * (1 - s/2).\n    let l = b * (1.0 - s / 2.0);\n    let sl = if l > 0.0 && l < 1.0 {\n        (b - l) / l.min(1.0 - l)\n    } else {\n        0.0\n    };\n\n    Some(ColorValue::new(h, sl, l, 1.0))\n}\n\n/// Parse a user-typed string into a [`ColorValue`].\n///\n/// Recognizes: `#rrggbb`, `#rrggbbaa`, `rgb(r,g,b)`, `rgba(r,g,b,a)`,\n/// `hsl(h,s%,l%)`, `hsla(h,s%,l%,a)`, and `hsb(h,s%,b%)`. Returns `None` for\n/// any unrecognized or malformed input.\n#[must_use]\npub fn parse_color_string(input: &str) -> Option<ColorValue> {\n    let trimmed = input.trim();\n    if trimmed.starts_with('#') {\n        return ColorValue::from_hex(trimmed);\n    }\n    if let Some(inner) = strip_fn_call(trimmed, \"rgba\") {\n        return parse_rgb_args(inner, true);\n    }\n    if let Some(inner) = strip_fn_call(trimmed, \"rgb\") {\n        return parse_rgb_args(inner, false);\n    }\n    if let Some(inner) = strip_fn_call(trimmed, \"hsla\") {\n        return parse_hsl_args(inner, true);\n    }\n    if let Some(inner) = strip_fn_call(trimmed, \"hsl\") {\n        return parse_hsl_args(inner, false);\n    }\n    if let Some(inner) = strip_fn_call(trimmed, \"hsb\") {\n        return parse_hsb_args(inner);\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Format a [`ColorValue`] as a string in the given format.\n#[must_use]\npub fn format_color_string(color: &ColorValue, format: ColorFormat) -> String {\n    match format {\n        ColorFormat::Hex => color.to_hex(color.alpha < 1.0),\n        ColorFormat::Rgb => {\n            let (r, g, b) = color.to_rgb();\n            if color.alpha < 1.0 {\n                format!(\"rgba({}, {}, {}, {:.2})\", r, g, b, color.alpha)\n            } else {\n                format!(\"rgb({r}, {g}, {b})\")\n            }\n        }\n        ColorFormat::Hsl => color.to_css_hsl(),\n        ColorFormat::Hsb => {\n            let (h, s, b) = color.to_hsb();\n            format!(\"hsb({:.0}, {:.1}%, {:.1}%)\", h, s * 100.0, b * 100.0)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// Round-trip helper: assert two RGB triples are within `tol` per channel.\n    fn rgb_close(a: (u8, u8, u8), b: (u8, u8, u8), tol: u8) {\n        assert!(\n            a.0.abs_diff(b.0) <= tol && a.1.abs_diff(b.1) <= tol && a.2.abs_diff(b.2) <= tol,\n            \"rgb {a:?} not within {tol} of {b:?}\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn default_is_pure_red() {\n        let c = ColorValue::default();\n        assert_eq!(c.to_rgb(), (255, 0, 0));\n        assert_eq!(c.alpha, 1.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn new_wraps_hue_and_clamps_channels() {\n        let c = ColorValue::new(400.0, 2.0, -1.0, 5.0);\n        assert!((c.hue - 40.0).abs() < 1e-9);\n        assert_eq!(c.saturation, 1.0);\n        assert_eq!(c.lightness, 0.0);\n        assert_eq!(c.alpha, 1.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn hsl_rgb_round_trip_primaries() {\n        for rgb in [\n            (255, 0, 0),\n            (0, 255, 0),\n            (0, 0, 255),\n            (255, 255, 0),\n            (0, 255, 255),\n            (255, 0, 255),\n            (128, 64, 32),\n        ] {\n            let c = ColorValue::from_rgb(rgb.0, rgb.1, rgb.2);\n            rgb_close(c.to_rgb(), rgb, 1);\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn hex_parse_and_format() {\n        let c = ColorValue::from_hex(\"#3366ff\").unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(c.to_rgb(), (0x33, 0x66, 0xff));\n        assert_eq!(c.to_hex(false), \"#3366ff\");\n\n        let with_alpha = ColorValue::from_hex(\"#3366ff80\").unwrap();\n        assert!((with_alpha.alpha - 128.0 / 255.0).abs() < 1e-9);\n        assert_eq!(with_alpha.to_hex(true), \"#3366ff80\");\n\n        assert_eq!(ColorValue::from_hex(\"nope\"), None);\n        assert_eq!(ColorValue::from_hex(\"#fff\"), None);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn parse_color_string_recognizes_all_formats() {\n        rgb_close(\n            parse_color_string(\"rgb(255, 0, 0)\").unwrap().to_rgb(),\n            (255, 0, 0),\n            1,\n        );\n        let rgba = parse_color_string(\"rgba(0, 0, 255, 0.5)\").unwrap();\n        rgb_close(rgba.to_rgb(), (0, 0, 255), 1);\n        assert!((rgba.alpha - 0.5).abs() < 1e-9);\n\n        rgb_close(\n            parse_color_string(\"hsl(120, 100%, 50%)\").unwrap().to_rgb(),\n            (0, 255, 0),\n            1,\n        );\n        let hsla = parse_color_string(\"hsla(0, 100%, 50%, 0.25)\").unwrap();\n        assert!((hsla.alpha - 0.25).abs() < 1e-9);\n\n        rgb_close(\n            parse_color_string(\"hsb(240, 100%, 100%)\").unwrap().to_rgb(),\n            (0, 0, 255),\n            1,\n        );\n\n        assert_eq!(parse_color_string(\"not a color\"), None);\n        assert_eq!(parse_color_string(\"rgb(1, 2)\"), None);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn format_color_string_per_format() {\n        let red = = black.contrast_ratio(&white);\n        assert!((ratio - 21.0).abs() < 0.1, \"ratio was {ratio}\");\n        assert!(black.passes_wcag_aaa(&white, false));\n 216	impl ColorValue {
217	    /// Compute the relative luminance per the WCAG 2.1 definition.
218	    ///
219	    /// Uses the sRGB linearization formula: if `C <= 0.04045`, `C / 12.92`;
220	    /// else `((C + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4`. Returns a value in `[0.0, 1.0]`.
221	    #[must_use]
222	    pub fn relative_luminance(&self) -> f64 {
223	        let (r, g, b) = self.to_rgb();
224	        0.2126 * srgb_to_linear(r) + 0.7152 * srgb_to_linear(g) + 0.0722 * srgb_to_linear(b)
225	    }
226	
227	    /// Compute the WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio between two colors.
228	    ///
229	    /// Returns a value in `[1.0, 21.0]`. Higher is more contrast.
230	    #[must_use]
231	    pub fn contrast_ratio(&self, other: &ColorValue) -> f64 {
232	        let l1 = self.relative_luminance();
233	        let l2 = other.relative_luminance();
234	        let (lighter, darker) = if l1 > l2 { (l1, l2) } else { (l2, l1) };
235	        (lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05)
236	    }
237	
238	    /// Check if this color passes WCAG AA contrast against another color.
239	    ///
240	    /// Normal text: 4.5:1; large text (>= 18pt or >= 14pt bold): 3:1.
241	    #[must_use]
242	    pub fn passes_wcag_aa(&self, other: &ColorValue, large_text: bool) -> bool {
243	        let ratio = self.contrast_ratio(other);
244	        if large_text {
245	            ratio >= 3.0
246	        } else {
247	            ratio >= 4.5
248	        }
249	    }
250	
251	    /// Check if this color passes WCAG AAA contrast against another color.
252	    ///
253	    /// Normal text: 7:1; large text: 4.5:1.
254	    #[must_use]
255	    pub fn passes_wcag_aaa(&self, other: &ColorValue, large_text: bool) -> bool {
256	        let ratio = self.contrast_ratio(other);
257	        if large_text {
258	            ratio >= 4.5
259	        } else {
260	            ratio >= 7.0
261	        }
262	    }
263	}

265	// ── Perceptual color naming ─────────────────────────────────────────────
266	
267	/// Describes a color in human-readable terms for screen readers.
268	///
269	/// Components: lightness modifier, chroma modifier, and hue name. Parts are
270	/// returned as `String` (not `&'static str`) so the i18n layer can substitute
271	/// localized labels. [`ColorValue::color_name_parts`] returns English keys; a
272	/// component's `format_name` message maps and orders them per locale.
273	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
274	pub struct ColorNameParts {
275	    /// e.g., "dark", "light", "very dark", "very light", or "" for medium.
276	    pub lightness: String,
277	    /// e.g., "vibrant", "pale", or "" for moderate.
278	    pub chroma: String,
279	    /// e.g., "red", "blue", "cyan-blue", "gray", "white", "black".
280	    pub hue: String,
281	}
282	
283	/// Map an OKLCH hue angle (degrees, 0-360) to one of 13 named hue buckets.
284	fn hue_name(h: f64) -> &'static str {
285	    match h {
286	        x if x < 35.0 => "red",
287	        x if x < 55.0 => "red-orange",
288	        x if x < 75.0 => "orange",
289	        x if x < 90.0 => "yellow-orange",
290	        x if x < 110.0 => "yellow",
291	        x if x < 135.0 => "yellow-green",
292	        x if x < 165.0 => "green",
293	        x if x < 185.0 => "cyan-green",
294	        x if x < 205.0 => "cyan",
295	        x if x < 240.0 => "cyan-blue",
296	        x if x < 280.0 => "blue",
297	        x if x < 320.0 => "purple",
298	        x if x < 350.0 => "magenta",
299	        _ => "red",
300	    }
301	}

303	impl ColorValue {
304	    /// Convert this color to OKLCH `(lightness, chroma, hue_degrees)`.
305	    ///
306	    /// OKLCH is a perceptually uniform space; classifying in it yields more
307	    /// natural color names than classifying in HSL. Uses Björn Ottosson's
308	    /// OKLab transform from linear sRGB.
309	    fn to_oklch(&self) -> (f64, f64, f64) {
310	        let (r, g, b) = self.to_rgb();
311	        let lr = srgb_to_linear(r);
312	        let lg = srgb_to_linear(g);
313	        let lb = srgb_to_linear(b);
314	
315	        let l = 0.412_221_470_8 * lr + 0.536_332_536_3 * lg + 0.051_445_992_9 * lb;
316	        let m = 0.211_903_498_2 * lr + 0.680_699_545_1 * lg + 0.107_396_956_6 * lb;
317	        let s = 0.088_302_461_9 * lr + 0.281_718_837_6 * lg + 0.629_978_700_5 * lb;
318	
319	        let l_ = l.cbrt();
320	        let m_ = m.cbrt();
321	        let s_ = s.cbrt();
322	
323	        let big_l = 0.210_454_255_3 * l_ + 0.793_617_785_0 * m_ - 0.004_072_046_8 * s_;
324	        let a = 1.977_998_495_1 * l_ - 2.428_592_205_0 * m_ + 0.450_593_709_9 * s_;
325	        let bb = 0.025_904_037_1 * l_ + 0.782_771_766_2 * m_ - 0.808_675_766_0 * s_;
326	
327	        let chroma = (a * a + bb * bb).sqrt();
328	        // atan2 returns radians in (-PI, PI]; convert to degrees and wrap to [0, 360).
329	        let hue = (bb.atan2(a) * (180.0 / core::f64::consts::PI)).rem_euclid(360.0);
330	        (big_l, chroma, hue)
331	    }
332	
333	    /// Returns English color description parts for accessibility.

470	///
471	/// The `ColorPicker` area targets two channels at once, while channel sliders
472	/// target a single channel.
473	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
474	pub enum DragTarget {
475	    /// 2D area: `x_channel = Saturation`, `y_channel = Lightness` (fixed in `ColorPicker`).
476	    Area,
477	    /// 1D channel slider.
478	    Channel(ColorChannel),
479	}
480	
481	// ── Channel helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
482	
483	/// Get the current value of a single channel from a [`ColorValue`].
484	#[must_use]
485	pub fn channel_value(color: &ColorValue, channel: ColorChannel) -> f64 {
486	    match channel {
487	        ColorChannel::Hue => color.hue,
488	        ColorChannel::Saturation => color.saturation,
489	        ColorChannel::Lightness => color.lightness,
490	        ColorChannel::Brightness => color.to_hsb().2,
491	        ColorChannel::Alpha => color.alpha,
492	        ColorChannel::Red => f64::from(color.to_rgb().0),
493	        ColorChannel::Green => f64::from(color.to_rgb().1),
494	        ColorChannel::Blue => f64::from(color.to_rgb().2),
495	    }
496	}
497	
498	/// Return a new [`ColorValue`] with one channel replaced.
499	#[must_use]
500	pub fn with_channel(color: &ColorValue, channel: ColorChannel, value: f64) -> ColorValue {
501	    match channel {
502	        ColorChannel::Hue => ColorValue::new(value, color.saturation, color.lightness, color.alpha),
503	        ColorChannel::Saturation => ColorValue::new(color.hue, value, color.lightness, color.alpha),
504	        ColorChannel::Lightness => ColorValue::new(color.hue, color.saturation, value, color.alpha),
505	        ColorChannel::Brightness => {
506	            // Convert current HSL to HSB, replace B, convert back.
507	            let (h, s_hsb, _) = color.to_hsb();
508	            let v = value.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
509	            let l = v * (1.0 - s_hsb / 2.0);
510	            let s_hsl = if l == 0.0 || l == 1.0 {
511	                0.0
512	            } else {
513	                (v - l) / l.min(1.0 - l)
514	            };
515	            ColorValue::new(h, s_hsl, l, color.alpha)
516	        }
517	        ColorChannel::Alpha => ColorValue::new(color.hue, color.saturation, color.lightness, value),
518	        ColorChannel::Red => {
519	            let (_, g, b) = color.to_rgb();
520	            let mut c = ColorValue::from_rgb(value.round() as u8, g, b);
521	            c.alpha = color.alpha;
522	            c
523	        }
524	        ColorChannel::Green => {
525	            let (r, _, b) = color.to_rgb();
526	            let mut c = ColorValue::from_rgb(r, value.round() as u8, b);
527	            c.alpha = color.alpha;
528	            c
529	        }
530	        ColorChannel::Blue => {
531	            let (r, g, _) = color.to_rgb();
532	            let mut c = ColorValue::from_rgb(r, g, value.round() as u8);
533	            c.alpha = color.alpha;
534	            c
535	        }
536	    }
537	}
538	
539	/// The `(min, max)` range for a channel.
540	#[must_use]
541	pub fn channel_range(channel: ColorChannel) -> (f64, f64) {
542	    match channel {
543	        ColorChannel::Hue => (0.0, 360.0),
544	        ColorChannel::Red | ColorChannel::Green | ColorChannel::Blue => (0.0, 255.0),
545	        // Saturation, Lightness, Brightness, Alpha
546	        _ => (0.0, 1.0),
547	    }
548	}
549	
550	/// The default step size for keyboard adjustment of a channel.
551	#[must_use]
552	pub fn channel_step_default(channel: ColorChannel) -> f64 {
553	    match channel {
554	        // 1 degree for hue, 1 unit for the 0-255 RGB channels.
555	        ColorChannel::Hue | ColorChannel::Red | ColorChannel::Green | ColorChannel::Blue => 1.0,
556	        // 1% for the 0..1 range channels.
557	        _ => 0.01,
558	    }
559	}

//! Property-based regression tests for [`AttrMap`] invariants.
//!
//! These tests are `#[ignore]`d so they do not run in the per-PR fast tier.
//! The nightly workflow runs them with
//! `cargo test -p ars-core -- --ignored proptest` and `PROPTEST_CASES=10000`
//! for extended coverage. Run locally with the same command at the default
//! `PROPTEST_CASES=256` budget to smoke-test the properties.
//!
//! Property coverage keeps a sorted-keys invariant and a set/get round-trip
//! on non-space-separated attributes — the two contracts `AttrMap::set` and
//! `AttrMap::get` rely on via `binary_search_by`. Space-separated attributes
//! (class, aria-labelledby, aria-controls, etc.) have append semantics and
//! are deliberately excluded from the simple round-trip property.

use ars_core::{AriaAttr, AttrMap, AttrValue, HtmlAttr};
use proptest::prelude::*;

/// Strategy: pick from a bounded set of single-value `HtmlAttr` keys.
///
/// These keys are not in [`SPACE_SEPARATED`] inside `ars_core::connect`, so
/// `set` performs replace semantics and `get` returns exactly what was set.
fn single_value_attr() -> impl Strategy<Value = HtmlAttr> {
    prop_oneof![
        Just(HtmlAttr::Role),
        Just(HtmlAttr::Id),
        Just(HtmlAttr::TabIndex),
        Just(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label)),
        Just(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Expanded)),
        Just(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Orientation)),
    ]
}

/// Strategy: short non-empty ASCII strings. The round-trip property only
/// requires that whatever goes in comes back unchanged, so the alphabet is
/// intentionally narrow to keep shrinking fast.
fn attr_string_value() -> impl Strategy<Value = String> {
    "[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,16}".prop_map(String::from)
}

########## spec_conformance/helper.rs ##########
//! Shared helpers for spec-conformance tests.
//!
//! Per-component tests call [`assert_anatomy`] with the expected scope and
//! the expected `(part, kebab-name)` list. The helper checks every facet
//! of the `ComponentPart` contract that the spec's §3 anatomy table
//! declares:
//!
//! 1. `Part::scope()` matches the spec's `data-ars-scope` token.
//! 2. `Part::all()` produces exactly the declared parts in the declared
//!    order.
//! 3. Every declared part round-trips through `Part::name()` with the
//!    declared kebab-case token.
//! 4. `Part::ROOT` equals the first declared part (workspace convention:
//!    every `Part` enum's first variant is `Root`).

use ars_core::ComponentPart;

/// Asserts that the supplied `Part` enum matches the spec's anatomy
/// declaration.
///
/// `expected_scope` is the `#[scope = "..."]` token the spec puts on the
/// `data-ars-scope` attribute. `expected_parts` is the ordered list of
/// `(part, kebab-name)` pairs from the spec's §3 anatomy table.
pub(crate) fn assert_anatomy<P>(expected_scope: &'static str, expected_parts: &[(P, &'static str)])
where
    P: ComponentPart + core::fmt::Debug + PartialEq,
{
    assert_eq!(
        P::scope(),
        expected_scope,
        "Part::scope() must match spec §3 anatomy",
    );

    let actual = P::all();

    let actual_names = actual.iter().map(ComponentPart::name).collect::<Vec<_>>();

    let expected_names = expected_parts
        .iter()
        .map(|(_, name)| *name)
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();

    assert_eq!(
        actual_names, expected_names,
        "Part::all() name list must equal spec §3 anatomy column \
         (scope = {expected_scope:?})",
    );

    assert_eq!(
        actual.len(),
        expected_parts.len(),
        "Part::all() length must match the number of spec §3 anatomy rows",
    );

    for (actual_part, (expected_part, expected_name)) in actual.iter().zip(expected_parts) {
        assert_eq!(
            actual_part.name(),
            *expected_name,
            "Part {actual_part:?} must produce kebab-name {expected_name:?}",
        );
        assert_eq!(
            actual_part, expected_part,
            "Part::all()[i] must equal the expected part value",
        );
    }

    if let Some((first_expected, _)) = expected_parts.first() {
        assert_eq!(
            &P::ROOT,
            first_expected,
            "Workspace convention: Part::ROOT (the first variant) must \
             equal the first spec-declared part",
        );
    }
}

//! Badge component connect API.
//!
//! `Badge` is a stateless, framework-agnostic attribute mapper for inline
//! status, count, category, and lifecycle labels.

use alloc::{format, string::String};
use core::fmt::{self, Debug};

use ars_core::{
    AriaAttr, AttrMap, ComponentMessages, ComponentPart, ConnectApi, Env, HtmlAttr, MessageFn,
};
use ars_i18n::{Locale, number};

type OverflowLabelFn = dyn Fn(u64, &Locale) -> String + Send + Sync;
type BadgeLabelFn = dyn Fn(u64, &str, &Locale) -> String + Send + Sync;

/// Props for the Badge component.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, ars_core::HasId)]
pub struct Props {
    /// Component instance ID.
    pub id: String,

    /// Visual style variant.
    pub variant: Variant,

    /// Visual size token.
    pub size: Size,

    /// Assistive-technology exposure mode.
    pub accessibility: Accessibility,

    /// Accessible label describing the badge content when visible text is not
    /// sufficient on its own.
    pub aria_label: Option<String>,
}

impl Default for Props {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            id: String::new(),
            variant: Variant::Subtle,
            size: Size::Sm,
            accessibility: Accessibility::Static,
            aria_label: None,
        }
    }
}

impl Props {
    /// Returns fresh badge props with the documented defaults.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    /// Sets the component instance ID.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn id(mut self, id: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.id = id.into();
        self
    }

    /// Sets the visual style variant.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn variant(mut self, value: Variant) -> Self {
        self.variant = value;
        self
    }

    /// Sets the visual size token.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn size(mut self, value: Size) -> Self {
        self.size = value;
        self
    }

    /// Sets how assistive technology should perceive the badge.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn accessibility(mut self, value: Accessibility) -> Self {
        self.accessibility = value;
        self
    }

    /// Sets the accessible label for the badge.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn aria_label(mut self, value: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.aria_label = Some(value.into());
        self
    }
}

/// How the badge is exposed to assistive technology.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum Accessibility {
    /// Static visible content with an optional `aria-label`.
    Static,

    /// Visual-only badge hidden from assistive technology.
    Decorative,

    /// Polite live-region badge for dynamic, non-urgent updates.
    Status,

    /// Assertive alert badge for urgent status changes.
    Alert,
}

impl Accessibility {
    /// Returns whether this mode hides the badge from assistive technology.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn is_decorative(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::Decorative)
    }
}

/// Visual style variant of the badge.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum Variant {
    /// Filled badge with the strongest emphasis.
    Solid,

    /// Soft tinted badge with low emphasis.
    Soft,

    /// Subtle tinted badge with low emphasis.
    Subtle,

    /// Badge with a visible surface/background treatment.
    Surface,

    /// Outlined badge with transparent or minimal fill.
    Outline,

    /// Plain text-like badge with minimal chrome.
    Plain,
}

impl Variant {
    /// Returns the `data-ars-variant` value for this variant.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Solid => "solid",
            Self::Soft => "soft",
            Self::Subtle => "subtle",
            Self::Surface => "surface",
            Self::Outline => "outline",
            Self::Plain => "plain",
        }
    }
}

/// Visual size token of the badge.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum Size {
    /// Extra-small badge size.
    Xs,

    /// Small badge size.
    Sm,

    /// Medium badge size.
    Md,

    /// Large badge size.
    Lg,

    /// Extra-large badge size.
    Xl,
}

impl Size {
    /// Returns the `data-ars-size` value for this size.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Xs => "xs",
            Self::Sm => "sm",
            Self::Md => "md",
            Self::Lg => "lg",
            Self::Xl => "xl",
        }
    }
}

/// Messages for the Badge component.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Messages {
    /// Returns the overflow label, receiving the count and current locale.
    pub overflow_label: MessageFn<OverflowLabelFn>,

    /// Returns the badge's accessible label using the count, semantic category,
    /// and current locale.
    pub badge_label: MessageFn<BadgeLabelFn>,
}

impl Default for Messages {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            overflow_label: MessageFn::new(|count: u64, locale: &Locale| {
                format_count(count, locale)
            }),
            badge_label: MessageFn::new(
                |count: u64, category: &str, _locale: &Locale| match count {
                    0 => format!("No unread {category}s"),
                    1 => format!("1 unread {category}"),
                    n => format!("{n} unread {category}s"),
                },
            ),
        }
    }
}

impl ComponentMessages for Messages {}

/// Structural parts exposed by the Badge connect API.
#[derive(ComponentPart)]
#[scope = "badge"]
pub enum Part {
    /// The root inline badge element.
    Root,
}

/// API for the Badge component.
pub struct Api {
    props: Props,
    locale: Locale,
    messages: Messages,
}

impl Debug for Api {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("badge::Api")
            .field("props", &self.props)
            .field("locale", &self.locale)
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

impl Api {
    /// Creates a new API for the badge.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn new(props: Props, env: &Env, messages: &Messages) -> Self {
        Self {
            props,
            locale: env.locale.clone(),
            messages: messages.clone(),
        }
    }

    /// Returns the overflow label for the given count, such as `"99+"`.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn overflow_label(&self, count: u64) -> String {
        (self.messages.overflow_label)(count, &self.locale)
    }

    /// Returns the badge's accessible label for a count and category.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn badge_label(&self, count: u64, category: &str) -> String {
        (self.messages.badge_label)(count, category, &self.locale)
    }

    /// Returns root attributes for the badge.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn root_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {
        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::Root.data_attrs();

        attrs
            .set(scope_attr, scope_val)
            .set(part_attr, part_val)
            .set(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-variant"), self.props.variant.as_str())
            .set(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-size"), self.props.size.as_str());

        match self.props.accessibility {
            Accessibility::Decorative => {
                attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Hidden), "true");
                return attrs;
            }

            Accessibility::Alert => {
                attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Role, "alert");
            }

            Accessibility::Status => {
                attrs
                    .set(HtmlAttr::Role, "status")
                    .set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Live), "polite");
            }

            Accessibility::Static => {}
        }

        if let Some(label) = &self.props.aria_label {
            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label), label.as_str());
        }

        attrs
    }

    /// Returns the badge accessibility mode.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn accessibility(&self) -> Accessibility {
        self.props.accessibility
    }

    /// Returns the badge aria-label override, when present.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn aria_label(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        self.props.aria_label.as_deref()
    }
}

impl ConnectApi for Api {
    type Part = Part;

    fn part_attrs(&self, part: Self::Part) -> AttrMap {
        match part {
            Part::Root => self.root_attrs(),
        }
    }
}

/// Formats a count value as locale-aware text with a maximum visible value of
/// `99+`.
#[must_use]
pub fn format_count(value: u64, locale: &Locale) -> String {
    let formatter = number::Formatter::new(locale, number::FormatOptions::default());

    if value > 99 {
        format!("{}+", formatter.format(99.0))
    } else {
        formatter.format(value as f64)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use ars_core::ConnectApi;
    use insta::assert_snapshot;

    use super::*;

    fn api(props: Props) -> Api {
        Api::new(props, &Env::default(), &Messages::default())
    }

    fn snapshot_attrs(attrs: &AttrMap) -> String {
        format!("{attrs:#?}")
    }

    #[test]
    fn props_builder_chain_applies_each_setter() {
        let props = Props::new()
            .id("badge-1")
            .variant(Variant::Outline)
            .size(Size::Xl)
            .accessibility(Accessibility::Alert)
            .aria_label("3 unread messages");

        assert_eq!(props.id, "badge-1");
        assert_eq!(props.variant, Variant::Outline);
        assert_eq!(props.size, Size::Xl);
        assert_eq!(props.accessibility, Accessibility::Alert);
        assert_eq!(props.aria_label.as_deref(), Some("3 unread messages"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn props_new_returns_default_values() {
        assert_eq!(Props::new(), Props::default());
    }

    #[test]
    fn accessibility_reports_decorative_mode() {
        assert!(Accessibility::Decorative.is_decorative());
        assert!(!Accessibility::Static.is_decorative());
        assert!(!Accessibility::Status.is_decorative());
        assert!(!Accessibility::Alert.is_decorative());
    }

    #[test]
    fn badge_root_default_snapshot() {
        assert_snapshot!(
            "badge_root_default",
            snapshot_attrs(&api(Props::new()).root_attrs())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn badge_root_status_snapshot() {
        assert_snapshot!(
            "badge_root_status",
            snapshot_attrs(
                &api(Props::new()
                    .accessibility(Accessibility::Status)
                    .aria_label("3 unread notifications"))
                .root_attrs()
            )
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn badge_root_alert_snapshot() {
        assert_snapshot!(
            "badge_root_alert",
            snapshot_attrs(
                &api(Props::new()
                    .accessibility(Accessibility::Alert)
                    .aria_label("Payment failed"))
                .root_attrs()
            )
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn badge_root_decorative_snapshot() {
        assert_snapshot!(
            "badge_root_decorative",
            snapshot_attrs(
                &api(Props::new()
                    .accessibility(Accessibility::Decorative)
                    .aria_label("Hidden"))
                .root_attrs()
            )
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_variant_emits_expected_data_attr() {
        let cases = [
            (Variant::Solid, "solid"),
            (Variant::Soft, "soft"),
            (Variant::Subtle, "subtle"),
            (Variant::Surface, "surface"),
            (Variant::Outline, "outline"),
            (Variant::Plain, "plain"),
        ];

        for (variant, expected) in cases {
            assert_eq!(variant.as_str(), expected);

            let attrs = api(Props::new().variant(variant)).root_attrs();

            assert_eq!(attrs.get(&HtmlAttr::Data("ars-variant")), Some(expected));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_size_emits_expected_data_attr() {
        let cases = [
            (Size::Xs, "xs"),
            (Size::Sm, "sm"),
            (Size::Md, "md"),
            (Size::Lg, "lg"),
            (Size::Xl, "xl"),
        ];

        for (size, expected) in cases {
            assert_eq!(size.as_str(), expected);

            let attrs = api(Props::new().size(size)).root_attrs();

            assert_eq!(attrs.get(&HtmlAttr::Data("ars-size")), Some(expected));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn status_attrs_set_status_live_and_label() {
        let attrs = api(Props::new()
            .accessibility(Accessibility::Status)
            .aria_label("3 unread messages"))
        .root_attrs();

        assert_eq!(attrs.get(&HtmlAttr::Role), Some("status"));
        assert_eq!(attrs.get(&HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Live)), Some("polite"));
        assert_eq!(
            attrs.get(&HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label)),
            Some("3 unread messages")
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn static_attrs_set_only_label_when_provided() {
        let attrs = api(Props::new().aria_label("Beta feature")).root_attrs();

        assert_eq!(
            attrs.get(&HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label)),
            Some("Beta feature")
        );
        assert!(!attrs.contains(&HtmlAttr::Role));
        assert!(!attrs.contains(&HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Live)));
        assert!(!attrs.contains(&HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Hidden)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn alert_attrs_set_alert_and_label() {
        let attrs = api(Props::new()
            .accessibility(Accessibility::Alert)
            .aria_label("Payment failed"))
        .root_attrs();

        assert_eq!(attrs.get(&HtmlAttr::Role), Some("alert"));
        assert_eq!(
            attrs.get(&HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label)),
            Some("Payment failed")
        );
        assert!(!attrs.contains(&HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Live)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn decorative_attrs_set_aria_hidden_and_suppress_all_a11y_semantics() {
        let attrs = api(Props::new()
            .accessibility(Accessibility::Decorative)
            .aria_label("Hidden"))
        .root_attrs();

        assert_eq!(attrs.get(&HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Hidden)), Some("true"));
        assert!(!attrs.contains(&HtmlAttr::Role));
        assert!(!attrs.contains(&HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Live)));
        assert!(!attrs.contains(&HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn api_exposes_accessibility_and_label() {
        let api = api(Props::new()
            .accessibility(Accessibility::Status)
            .aria_label("3 unread messages"));

        assert_eq!(api.accessibility(), Accessibility::Status);
        assert_eq!(api.aria_label(), Some("3 unread messages"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn api_debug_is_stable_and_redacts_messages() {
        let api = api(Props::new()
            .id("badge-1")
            .accessibility(Accessibility::Status));

        let debug = format!("{api:?}");

        assert!(debug.contains("badge::Api"));
        assert!(debug.contains("badge-1"));
        assert!(debug.contains("Status"));
        assert!(debug.contains("locale"));
        assert!(!debug.contains("messages"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn part_attrs_delegates_to_root_attrs() {
        let api = api(Props::new().variant(Variant::Solid));

        assert_eq!(api.part_attrs(Part::Root), api.root_attrs());
    }

    #[test]
    fn message_helpers_return_overflow_and_accessible_labels() {
        let messages = Messages {
            overflow_label: MessageFn::new(|count: u64, _locale: &Locale| {
                format!("more than {count}")
            }),
            badge_label: MessageFn::new(|count: u64, category: &str, _locale: &Locale| {
                format!("{count} {category} ready")
            }),
        };

        let api = Api::new(Props::new(), &Env::default(), &messages);

        assert_eq!(api.overflow_label(99), "more than 99");
        assert_eq!(api.badge_label(3, "notification"), "3 notification ready");
    }

    #[test]
    fn default_badge_label_handles_zero_one_and_plural_counts() {
        let api = api(Props::new());

        assert_eq!(
            api.badge_label(0, "notification"),
            "No unread notifications"
        );
        assert_eq!(api.badge_label(1, "notification"), "1 unread notification");
        assert_eq!(api.badge_label(2, "notification"), "2 unread notifications");
    }

    #[test]
    fn default_overflow_label_uses_capped_count_formatting() {
        let api = api(Props::new());

        assert_eq!(api.overflow_label(100), "99+");
    }

    #[test]
    fn format_count_caps_at_99_plus() {
        let locale = Env::default().locale;

        assert_eq!(format_count(0, &locale), "0");
        assert_eq!(format_count(99, &locale), "99");
        assert_eq!(format_count(100, &locale), "99+");
    }
}

When non-empty it is emitted as the root `id`.\n    pub id: String,\n    /// The color to display.\n    pub color: ColorValue,\n    /// Optional override for the auto-generated accessible color name.\n    ///\n    /// When `None`, the name is derived from\n    /// [`ColorValue::color_name_parts`] + [`Messages::format_name`].\n    pub color_name: Option<String>,\n    /// Whether to visually represent the alpha channel (checkerboard pattern).\n    pub respect_alpha: bool,\n}\n\nimpl Default for Props {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            id: String::new(),\n            color: ColorValue::default(),\n            color_name: None,\n            respect_alpha: true,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Messages for the `ColorSwatch` component.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug)]\npub struct Messages {\n    /// Formats the color name parts into a localized string.\n    ///\n    /// Default (en): `\"{lightness} {chroma} {hue}\"` — non-empty parts joined by\n    /// spaces. Other locales may reorder the parts.\n    pub format_name: MessageFn<FormatNameFn>,\n    /// Role description for the swatch element (default: `\"color swatch\"`).\n    pub role_description: MessageFn<RoleDescriptionFn>,\n}\n\nimpl Default for Messages {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            format_name: MessageFn::new(|parts: &ColorNameParts, _locale: &Locale| {\n                [\n                    parts.lightness.as_str(),\n                    parts.chroma.as_str(),\n                    parts.hue.as_str(),\n                ]\n                .into_iter()\n                .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())\n                .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                .join(\" \")\n            }),\n            role_description: MessageFn::static_str(\"color swatch\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl ComponentMessages for Messages {}\n\n/// Structural parts exposed by the `ColorSwatch` connect API.\n#[derive(ComponentPart)]\n#[scope = \"color-swatch\"]\npub enum Part {\n    /// Container with `role=\"img\"` and the accessible color name.\n    Root,\n    /// Color fill element, with an optional checkerboard for alpha.\n    Inner,\n}\n\n/// API for the `ColorSwatch` component.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct Api<'a> {\n    props: &'a Props,\n    locale: Locale,\n    messages: Messages,\n}\n\nimpl<'a> Api<'a> {\n    /// Creates a new API for the swatch.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn new(props: &'a Props, env: &Env, messages: &Messages) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            props,\n            locale: env.locale.clone(),\n            messages: messages.clone(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The resolved accessible color name — either the explicit override or the\n    /// auto-generated perceptual name.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn color_name(&self) -> String {\n        if let Some(name) = &self.props.color_name {\n            name.clone()\n        } else {\n            let parts = self.props.color.color_name_parts();\n            (self.messages.format_name)(&parts, &self.locale)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Attributes for the root element.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn root_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();\n        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::Root.data_attrs();\n        attrs.set(scope_attr, scope_val).set(part_attr, part_val);\n        if !self.props.id.is_empty() {\n            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Id, self.props.id.clone());\n        }\n        attrs\n            .set(HtmlAttr::Role, \"img\")\n            .set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label), self.color_name())\n            .set(\n                HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::RoleDescription),\n                (self.messages.role_description)(&self.locale),\n            )\n            .set_style(\n                CssProperty::Custom(\"ars-swatch-color\"),\n                self.props.color.to_css_hsl(),\n            );\n        attrs\n    }\n\n    /// Attributes for the inner color-fill element.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn inner_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();\n        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::Inner.data_attrs();\n        attrs\n            .set(scope_attr, scope_val)\n            .set(part_attr, part_val)\n            .set_style(CssProperty::Background, self.props.color.to_css_hsl());\n        if self.props.respect_alpha && self.props.color.alpha < 1.0 {\n            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-alpha\"), true);\n        }\n        attrs\n    }\n}\n\nimpl ConnectApi for Api<'_> {\n    type Part = Part;\n\n    fn part_attrs(&self, part: Part) -> AttrMap {\n        match part {\n            Part::Root => alloc::format!(\"{attrs:#?}\")\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn renders_color_sample_with_img_role_and_label() {\n        let props = Props {\n            color: ColorValue::from_rgb(0, 0, 255),\n 547	    /// The attributes for the root element.
548	    pub fn root_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {
549	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
550	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::Root.data_attrs();
551	        attrs.set(scope_attr, scope_val);
552	        attrs.set(part_attr, part_val);
553	        if self.ctx.disabled {
554	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-disabled"), true);
555	        }
556	        if self.ctx.readonly {
557	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-readonly"), true);
558	        }
559	        if self.ctx.invalid {
560	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-invalid"), true);
561	        }
562	        if self.ctx.focused {
563	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-focused"), true);
564	        }
565	        if self.ctx.focus_visible {
566	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-focus-visible"), true);
567	        }

569	    }
570	
571	    /// The attributes for the label element.
572	    pub fn label_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {
573	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
574	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::Label.data_attrs();
575	        attrs.set(scope_attr, scope_val);
576	        attrs.set(part_attr, part_val);
577	        let label_id = self.ctx.ids.part("label");
578	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Id, label_id);
579	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::For, self.ctx.ids.part("input"));
580	        attrs
581	    }
582	
583	    /// The attributes for the input element.
584	    pub fn input_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {
585	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
586	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::Input.data_attrs();
587	        attrs.set(scope_attr, scope_val);
588	        attrs.set(part_attr, part_val);
589	        let input_id = self.ctx.ids.part("input");
590	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Id, input_id);
591	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Type, "text");
592	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Value, &self.ctx.input_text);
593	
594	        // Mode-specific ARIA
595	        match self.ctx.channel {
596	            Some(ch) => {
597	                // Channel mode: numeric spinbutton
598	                attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Role, "spinbutton");
599	                attrs.set(HtmlAttr::InputMode, "numeric");
600	                if let Some(color) = self.ctx.value.get() {
601	                    let val = channel_value(color, ch);
602	                    let (min, max) = channel_range(ch);
603	                    attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::ValueNow), format!("{:.2}", val));
604	                    attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::ValueMin), format!("{:.2}", min));
605	                    attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::ValueMax), format!("{:.2}", max));
606	                    attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::ValueText),
607	                        (self.ctx.messages.channel_value_text)(ch, val, &self.ctx.locale));
608	                }
609	                attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label),
610	                    (self.ctx.messages.channel_label)(ch, &self.ctx.locale));
611	            }
612	            None => {
613	                // Whole-color mode: standard text input
614	                attrs.set(HtmlAttr::InputMode, "text");
615	                attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label),
616	                    (self.ctx.messages.color_label)(&self.ctx.locale));
617	            }
618	        }
619	
620	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::LabelledBy), self.ctx.ids.part("label"));
621	
622	        if self.ctx.invalid {
623	            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Invalid), "true");
624	        }
625	        if self.ctx.required {
626	            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Required), "true");
627	        }
628	        if self.ctx.readonly {
629	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::ReadOnly), true);
630	        }
631	        if self.ctx.disabled {
632	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Disabled, true);
633	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Disabled), true);
634	        }
635	
636	        // describedby: description + error message
637	        let mut describedby = Vec::new();
638	        if self.ctx.has_description {
639	            describedby.push(self.ctx.ids.part("description"));
640	        }
641	        if self.ctx.invalid {
642	            describedby.push(self.ctx.ids.part("error-message"));
643	        }
644	        if !describedby.is_empty() {
645	            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::DescribedBy), describedby.join(" "));
646	        }
647	
648	        attrs
649	    }

711	    /// Handle keydown on the input element.
712	    pub fn on_input_keydown(&self, data: &KeyboardEventData) {
713	        if self.ctx.is_composing { return; }
714	        match data.key {
715	            KeyboardKey::Enter => (self.send)(Event::Commit),
716	            KeyboardKey::ArrowUp if self.ctx.channel.is_some() => (self.send)(Event::Increment),
717	            KeyboardKey::ArrowDown if self.ctx.channel.is_some() => (self.send)(Event::Decrement),
718	            KeyboardKey::PageUp if self.ctx.channel.is_some() => (self.send)(Event::IncrementLarge),
719	            KeyboardKey::PageDown if self.ctx.channel.is_some() => (self.send)(Event::DecrementLarge),
720	            KeyboardKey::Home if self.ctx.channel.is_some() => (self.send)(Event::DecrementToMin),
721	            KeyboardKey::End if self.ctx.channel.is_some() => (self.send)(Event::IncrementToMax),
722	            _ => {}
723	        }
724	    }
725

727	    pub fn on_composition_start(&self) {
728	        (self.send)(Event::CompositionStart);
729	    }
730

732	    pub fn on_composition_end(&self) {
733	        (self.send)(Event::CompositionEnd);
734	    }
735	}
