565	mod tests {
566	    use alloc::vec;
567	
568	    use ars_core::Service;
569	    use insta::assert_snapshot;
570	
571	    use super::*;
572	
573	    fn palette() -> Vec<ColorValue> {
574	        vec![
575	            ColorValue::from_rgb(255, 0, 0),
576	            ColorValue::from_rgb(0, 255, 0),
577	            ColorValue::from_rgb(0, 0, 255),
578	            ColorValue::from_rgb(255, 255, 0),
579	            ColorValue::from_rgb(0, 255, 255),
580	            ColorValue::from_rgb(255, 0, 255),
581	        ]
582	    }
583	
584	    fn service(mut props: Props) -> Service<Machine> {
585	        if props.id.is_empty() {
586	            props.id = "color-swatch-picker".to_string();
587	        }
588	
589	        Service::<Machine>::new(props, &Env::default(), &Messages::default())
590	    }
591	
592	    fn snapshot_attrs(attrs: &AttrMap) -> String {
593	        alloc::format!("{attrs:#?}")
594	    }
595	
596	    fn key(key: KeyboardKey) -> KeyboardEventData {
597	        KeyboardEventData {
598	            key,
599	            character: None,
600	            code: String::new(),
601	            shift_key: false,
602	            ctrl_key: false,
603	            alt_key: false,
604	            meta_key: false,
605	            repeat: false,
606	            is_composing: false,
607	        }
608	    }
609	
610	    #[test]
611	    fn root_is_listbox_with_label() {
612	        let svc = service(Props {
613	            colors: palette(),
614	            ..Props::default()
615	        });
616	
617	        let root = svc.connect(&|_| {}).root_attrs();
618	
619	        assert_eq!(root.get(&HtmlAttr::Role), Some("listbox"));
620	        assert_eq!(
621	            root.get(&HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label)),
622	            Some("Color swatches")
623	        );
624	    }
625	
626	    #[test]
627	    fn stack_layout_sets_horizontal_orientation_grid_does_not() {
628	        let stack = service(Props {
629	            colors: palette(),
630	            layout: SwatchPickerLayout::Stack,
631	            ..Props::default()
632	        });
633	
634	        assert_eq!(
635	            stack
636	                .connect(&|_| {})
637	                .root_attrs()
638	                .get(&HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Orientation)),
639	            Some("horizontal")
640	        );
641	
642	        let grid = service(Props {
643	            colors: palette(),
644	            ..Props::default()
645	        });
646	
647	        assert!(
648	            !grid
649	                .connect(&|_| {})
650	                .root_attrs()
651	                .contains(&HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Orientation))
652	        );
653	    }
654	
655	    #[test]
656	    fn item_exposes_option_role_selected_and_roving_tabindex() {
657	        let svc = service(Props {
658	            colors: palette(),
659	            default_value: ColorValue::from_rgb(0, 0, 255),
660	            ..Props::default()
661	        });
662	
663	        let api = svc.connect(&|_| {});
664	
665	        // Index 2 is blue, the selected value.
666	        let selected = api.item_attrs(2);
667	
668	        assert_eq!(selected.get(&HtmlAttr::Role), Some("option"));
669	        assert_eq!(
670	            selected.get(&HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Selected)),
671	            Some("true")
672	        );
673	
674	        // A non-selected item.
675	        let other = api.item_attrs(0);
676	
677	        assert_eq!(
678	            other.get(&HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Selected)),
679	            Some("false")
680	        );
681	        assert_eq!(other.get(&HtmlAttr::TabIndex), Some("-1"));
682	    }

684	    #[test]
685	    fn selecting_an_item_sets_value() {
686	        let mut svc = service(Props {
687	            colors: palette(),
688	            ..Props::default()
689	        });
690	
691	        drop(svc.send(Event::Select { index: 3 }));
692	
693	        assert_eq!(svc.connect(&|_| {}).value().to_rgb(), (255, 255, 0));
694	        assert_eq!(svc.connect(&|_| {}).focused_index(), Some(3));

697	    #[test]
698	    fn keyboard_navigation_moves_focus_in_grid() {
699	        let mut svc = service(Props {
700	            colors: palette(),
701	            columns: 3,
702	            ..Props::default()
703	        });
704	
705	        drop(svc.send(Event::Focus { is_keyboard: true }));
706	
707	        assert_eq!(svc.connect(&|_| {}).focused_index(), Some(0));
708	
709	        let captured = core::cell::RefCell::new(vec![]);
710	        let send = |event: Event| captured.borrow_mut().push(event);
711	
712	        let api = svc.connect(&send);
713	
714	        api.on_keydown(&key(KeyboardKey::ArrowDown));
715	
716	        assert!(matches!(captured.borrow()[0], Event::FocusDown));
717	    }

719	    #[test]
720	    fn grid_focus_down_wraps_by_columns() {
721	        let mut svc = service(Props {
722	            colors: palette(),
723	            columns: 3,
724	            ..Props::default()
725	        });
726	
727	        drop(svc.send(Event::Focus { is_keyboard: true }));
728	        drop(svc.send(Event::FocusDown));
729	
730	        // 0 + 3 columns -> index 3.
731	        assert_eq!(svc.connect(&|_| {}).focused_index(), Some(3));
732	    }

  "new_string": "    /// The index of the currently focused swatch, if any.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub const fn focused_index(&self) -> Option<usize> {\n        self.ctx.focused_index\n    }\n\n    /// The index of the single roving-tabbable swatch.\n    ///\n    /// While a swatch is focused this is the focused index. In the idle state\n    /// (`focused_index == None`) it is the selected swatch, or the first swatch\n    /// when nothing is selected, so the picker is reachable with the Tab key\n    /// before focus has entered it. Returns `None` only when the picker is\n    /// disabled or empty (every item then stays `tabindex=\"-1\"`).\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn tabbable_index(&self) -> Option<usize> {\n        if self.ctx.disabled || self.ctx.colors.is_empty() {\n            return None;\n        }\n\n        if let Some(index) = self.ctx.focused_index {\n            return Some(index);\n        }\n\n        let value = *self.ctx.value.get();\n        let selected = self\n            .ctx\n            .colors\n            .iter()\n            .position(|candidate| *candidate == value);\n\n        Some(selected.unwrap_or(0))\n    }"
}

  "new_string": "    fn transition(\n        state: &Self::State,\n        event: &Self::Event,\n        ctx: &Self::Context,\n        props: &Self::Props,\n    ) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Self>> {\n        // Parent-driven prop syncs always apply, even when disabled or empty, so\n        // the picker can be re-enabled or populated; everything else is ignored\n        // in those states.\n        let is_prop_sync = matches!(event, Event::SyncValue(_) | Event::SetProps);\n\n        if !is_prop_sync && (ctx.disabled || ctx.colors.is_empty()) {\n            return None;\n        }\n\n        match event {\n            Event::SyncValue(value) => {\n                let value = *value;\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(\n                    move |ctx: &mut Context| match value {\n                        Some(color) => {\n                            ctx.value.set(color);\n                            ctx.value.sync_controlled(Some(color));\n                        }\n                        None => ctx.value.sync_controlled(None),\n                    },\n                ))\n            }\n\n            Event::SetProps => {\n                let props = props.clone();\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n                    ctx.colors = props.colors.clone();\n                    ctx.layout = props.layout;\n                    ctx.columns = props.columns;\n                    ctx.disabled = props.disabled;\n\n                    // Drop focus if it now points past the (possibly shorter) list.\n                    if ctx.focused_index.is_some_and(|index| index >= ctx.colors.len()) {\n                        ctx.focused_index = None;\n                    }\n                }))\n            }\n\n            Event::Focus { is_keyboard } => {"

  "new_string": "    fn on_props_changed(old: &Props, new: &Props) -> Vec<Event> {\n        assert_eq!(\n            old.id, new.id,\n            \"color_swatch_picker::Props.id must remain stable after init\"\n        );\n\n        let mut events = Vec::new();\n\n        if old.value != new.value {\n            events.push(Event::SyncValue(new.value));\n        }\n\n        if props_output_changed(old, new) {\n            events.push(Event::SetProps);\n        }\n\n        events\n    }\n\n    fn connect<'a>(\n        state: &'a Self::State,\n        ctx: &'a Self::Context,\n        props: &'a Self::Props,\n        send: &'a dyn Fn(Self::Event),\n    ) -> Self::Api<'a> {\n        Api {\n            state,\n            ctx,\n            props,\n            send,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Whether any cached output prop changed and the context needs refreshing.\n///\n/// `name` is omitted: it is read live from `Props` in `hidden_input_attrs`\n/// rather than cached in the context.\nfn props_output_changed(old: &Props, new: &Props) -> bool {\n    old.colors != new.colors\n        || old.layout != new.layout\n        || old.columns != new.columns\n        || old.disabled != new.disabled\n}\n\n/// Structural parts exposed by the `ColorSwatchPicker` connect API."

I've addressed all 8 Codex findings and the loop is now watching for Codex's next pass. Summary of what landed on PR #698 (commit `1167c8bf`):

## Findings fixed (TDD, all in this PR)

**P1**
- **Controlled-mode prop sync** — added `on_props_changed` + `SyncValue`/`SetProps` events to all 6 color machines (slider, area, wheel, angle-slider, field, swatch-picker). Controlled `value`/`disabled`/`readonly`/etc. now apply after mount instead of going stale until remount. Disabled guards were restructured to still accept parent syncs (so a control can be re-enabled).
- **Percentage scaling** — `color_field` now divides percentage channels by 100 before clamping, so blurring a 50% saturation field commits 0.5, not 100%.

**P2**
- **Non-finite rejection** — `parse_finite_f64` makes `hsl(NaN,…)`/`hsl(inf,…)` return `None` instead of debug-panicking / leaking NaN.
- **Pending drag value** — new `Bindable::pending()`; drag `on_change_end` reports the just-dragged value in controlled mode.
- **Idle keyboard focus** — `color_swatch_picker::tabbable_index()` makes the selected/first swatch `tabindex=0` so users can Tab in.
- **Perceptual valuetext** — `color_area` threads `color_name_en()` into `aria-valuetext` (e.g. "light vibrant green, …").
- **Readonly enforcement** — `color_field` sets native `readonly` and ignores Change/blur-commit while readonly.
- **Disabled hidden inputs** — all hidden form inputs mirror `disabled`.

## Verification
- New tests for every finding; 2 snapshots updated (intentional: area valuetext, swatch idle tabindex).
- Specs synced across all 6 color files + `Bindable::pending` in foundation; `cargo xtask spec validate` clean.
- **`cargo xci-fast`: all 10 gates pass** (including `spec-compile-snippets`).
- All 8 threads replied with the fix + test name, and resolved.

`@codex review` re-triggered; the background watcher (`b66ceoguk`) will notify me when Codex either 👍s or posts new findings, and I'll continue the loop.

    /// Parse a hex string (`#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`).
    ///
    /// Returns `None` for any string whose hex digit count is neither 6 nor 8
    /// or that contains non-hex characters.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn from_hex(hex: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        let hex = hex.trim_start_matches('#');

        match hex.len() {
            6 => {
                let red = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[0..2], 16).ok()?;
                let green = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[2..4], 16).ok()?;
                let blue = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[4..6], 16).ok()?;

                Some(Self::from_rgb(red, green, blue))
            }

            8 => {
                let red = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[0..2], 16).ok()?;
                let green = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[2..4], 16).ok()?;
                let blue = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[4..6], 16).ok()?;
                let alpha_byte = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[6..8], 16).ok()?;

                let mut color = Self::from_rgb(red, green, blue);

                color.alpha = f64::from(alpha_byte) / 255.0;

                Some(color)
            }

PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F6IZA	crates/ars-core/src/color.rs:212	dbid=3329558268
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject extra leading hex markers**

When `ColorField` commits a whole-color value like `##3366ff`, `parse_color_string` routes it here and `trim_start_matches('#')` removes both markers, so the malformed user input is accepted as `#3366ff` instead of setting the field invalid. This should strip at most one optional leading `#` (or require exactly one in the parser path) so extra markers are rejected.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F6IZB	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_slider/mod.rs:663	dbid=3329558269
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep disabled color thumbs out of tab order**

When `Props.disabled` is true, the slider state machine ignores value-changing input, but this thumb still renders `tabindex="0"` and does not expose `aria-disabled`, leaving keyboard users able to tab to a dead control. The existing numeric slider gates the thumb tab index on `ctx.disabled`; please do the same here (and for the matching new color-area/color-wheel thumb attrs that use the same unconditional tab stop).

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F6IZD	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_slider/mod.rs:395	dbid=3329558271
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the hue slider's max endpoint**

When this slider controls `ColorChannel::Hue`, pressing End or dragging to the far end sets `max == 360`, but `with_channel` routes that through `ColorValue::new`, which wraps hue `360` back to `0`. The result is that the thumb and `aria-valuenow` jump to the minimum even though the user selected the maximum endpoint; handle the hue max endpoint explicitly or avoid using the wrapped stored hue as the slider position.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F6IZE	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_field/mod.rs:872	dbid=3329558272
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Always emit spinbutton value metadata**

With the default `Props::default_value == None`, setting only `channel: Some(...)` renders a `role="spinbutton"` but skips `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-valuetext`; keyboard adjustments and channel commits also no-op because they require an existing color. A channel field should either initialize a base color in channel mode or still expose/maintain a valid channel value so the spinbutton is usable and accessible.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F6IZF	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/angle_slider/mod.rs:342	dbid=3329558273
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp angle value after bounds prop changes**

When a parent changes `min`/`max` without also changing `value`, this only caches the new bounds and leaves the existing angle untouched, so a value that is now out of range continues to render as `aria-valuenow` and submit through the hidden input until the next user interaction. Re-clamp/snap `ctx.value` after updating these props so the exposed slider value remains within the current bounds.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F6IZG	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_wheel/mod.rs:568	dbid=3329558275
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove the dangling color wheel label reference**

The color wheel does not expose a `Label` part or `label_attrs`, but the thumb still sets `aria-labelledby` to a generated `*-label` id. In the rendered component that IDREF has no target, which can leave the slider's accessible name dependent on invalid markup instead of the `aria-label` set just above; either add/render a real label part or drop this `aria-labelledby`.

=== ColorValue::new + hue normalization ===
    /// Hue is wrapped into `[0, 360)`; saturation, lightness, and alpha are
    /// clamped to `[0.0, 1.0]`.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn new(hue: f64, saturation: f64, lightness: f64, alpha: f64) -> Self {

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stop readonly drags from mutating ColorArea**

If `readonly` is turned on while a drag is already in progress, the next `DragMove` still applies `apply_area_position` because only `DragStart` and keyboard-style events check `ctx.readonly`. This lets a read-only `ColorArea` continue changing its color until `DragEnd`, unlike the disabled path and `ColorWheel`'s shared disabled/readonly guard; guard `DragMove` as well while still allowing `DragEnd` to clean up the drag state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F8d16	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_slider/mod.rs:358	dbid=3330340629
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stop readonly drags from mutating ColorSlider**

When the parent sets `readonly` during an active drag, this `DragMove` branch keeps calling `apply_slider_position` because the read-only checks only cover `DragStart` and keyboard/set-to-min/max events. In that scenario the control is visibly read-only but still updates its channel value until pointer release; mirror the disabled handling by blocking value-changing `DragMove` events while still allowing `DragEnd` to finish the interaction.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve hue-axis endpoints in ColorArea**

When `ColorArea` is configured with `x_channel: Hue`, a pointer at the right edge produces `x_val == 360` from `channel_range`, but passing that through `with_channel` normalizes the stored `ColorValue.hue` to `0`. The next render then computes the thumb position and ARIA reading from `channel_value` as the minimum, so dragging to the max endpoint (and the analogous keyboard max paths) jumps back to 0 instead of exposing 360. Preserve the axis value separately or special-case the hue max endpoint.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F8jDj	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_field/mod.rs:990	dbid=3330367685
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stop submitting stale values for invalid color fields**

When a whole-color field already has a valid value and the user commits an invalid string, `commit_input` leaves `ctx.value` at the previous color while setting `invalid = true`; because the hidden form input still emits that previous hex value, a form submit sends a stale color that no longer matches the visible input. In the invalid state, omit/disable the hidden value or otherwise prevent submitting the last valid color as if it were current.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F8jDk	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_field/mod.rs:465	dbid=3330367687
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep inert color fields from accepting IME edits**

When a color field is read-only while composing, or becomes disabled mid-composition, this branch handles `Change` before the read-only/disabled guards below, so the inert field can still replace `input_text`. That leaves the visible text editable even though the later guard says disabled fields ignore edits and the normal `Change` path rejects read-only input; check inert state before accepting composition changes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
```

  "old_string": "/// Apply normalized `(x, y)` coordinates to both channels (y is inverted: top = max).\nfn apply_area_position(ctx: &mut Context, x: f64, y: f64) {\n    let color = *ctx.value.get();\n\n    let (x_min, x_max) = channel_range(ctx.x_channel);\n    let (y_min, y_max) = channel_range(ctx.y_channel);\n\n    let x_val = x_min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (x_max - x_min);\n    let y_val = y_max - y.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (y_max - y_min);\n\n    let updated = with_channel(&color, ctx.x_channel, x_val);\n\n    ctx.value.set(with_channel(&updated, ctx.y_channel, y_val));\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Apply normalized `(x, y)` coordinates to both channels (y is inverted: top = max).\nfn apply_area_position(ctx: &mut Context, x: f64, y: f64) {\n    let (x_min, x_max) = channel_range(ctx.x_channel);\n    let (y_min, y_max) = channel_range(ctx.y_channel);\n\n    let x_val = x_min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (x_max - x_min);\n    let y_val = y_max - y.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (y_max - y_min);\n\n    set_x_value(ctx, x_val);\n    set_y_value(ctx, y_val);\n}\n\n/// Set the x-axis channel value (unwrapped) and derive the color from it.\nfn set_x_value(ctx: &mut Context, value: f64) {\n    ctx.x_value = value;\n\n    let color = *ctx.value.get();\n    ctx.value.set(with_channel(&color, ctx.x_channel, value));\n}\n\n/// Set the y-axis channel value (unwrapped) and derive the color from it.\nfn set_y_value(ctx: &mut Context, value: f64) {\n    ctx.y_value = value;\n\n    let color = *ctx.value.get();\n    ctx.value.set(with_channel(&color, ctx.y_channel, value));\n}"
}

  "new_string": "/// Apply normalized `(x, y)` coordinates to both channels (y is inverted: top = max).\nfn apply_area_position(ctx: &mut Context, x: f64, y: f64) {\n    let (x_min, x_max) = channel_range(ctx.x_channel);\n    let (y_min, y_max) = channel_range(ctx.y_channel);\n\n    let x_val = x_min + x.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (x_max - x_min);\n    let y_val = y_max - y.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (y_max - y_min);\n\n    ctx.x_value = x_val;\n    ctx.y_value = y_val;\n\n    // Apply both channels from a single base color. Reading the bindable twice\n    // (as two `set_*_value` calls would) discards the first change in controlled\n    // mode, where `get()` keeps returning the controlled color.\n    let color = *ctx.value.get();\n    let updated = with_channel(&color, ctx.x_channel, x_val);\n    ctx.value.set(with_channel(&updated, ctx.y_channel, y_val));\n}"
}

        // During IME composition, suppress all keyboard shortcuts. Parent-driven

        if ctx.is_composing {

    pub fn hidden_input_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {
        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::HiddenInput.data_attrs();
        attrs.set(scope_attr, scope_val);
        attrs.set(part_attr, part_val);
        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Type, "hidden");
        if let Some(ref name) = self.ctx.name {
            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Name, name);
        }
        // Only submit a value when the field is valid. While invalid, the stored
        // color is the last *valid* value, which no longer matches the visible
        // input — submitting it would send a stale color.
        if let Some(color) = (*self.ctx.value.get()).filter(|_| !self.ctx.invalid) {
            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Value, color.to_hex(true));
        }
        // A disabled control must be omitted from form submission.
        if self.ctx.disabled {
            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Disabled, true);
        }
        attrs
    }

    // --- Event dispatch helpers ---

    /// The on input focus handler.
    pub fn on_input_focus(&self, is_keyboard: bool) {
        (self.send)(Event::Focus { is_keyboard });

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scale spinbutton ARIA values to match percentage input**

When `ch` is `Saturation`, `Lightness`, `Brightness`, or `Alpha`, `format_value` renders the input as a 0–100 percentage and `commit_input` parses that same 0–100 value by dividing by 100, but these `aria-valuenow/min/max` attributes still expose the underlying 0–1 range. A 50% saturation field therefore displays and accepts `50` while assistive tech sees `valuenow=0.50` in a `0.00..1.00` range; scale the ARIA numeric values by 100 for percentage channels so the spinbutton semantics match the visible control.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F8tCD	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_swatch_picker/mod.rs:301	dbid=3330422297
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clear focused item state on blur**

After a swatch receives focus and the picker blurs, this transition clears the focus flags but leaves `focused_index` set. `item_attrs` treats any matching `focused_index` as focused, so the previously focused option keeps `data-ars-focused` while the root is already back in the idle state; clear `focused_index` on blur or gate focused styling on `State::Focused` to avoid stale focus UI after tabbing away.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F8tCI	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_wheel/mod.rs:389	dbid=3330422303
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve ColorValue hue normalization at the max endpoint**

When users press End or dispatch `SetToMax`, this writes `hue: 360.0` directly into `ColorValue`, bypassing `ColorValue::new`'s normalization and violating the type's documented `[0, 360)` hue invariant. Consumers reading `ColorWheel::Api::value()` after that interaction can observe a `ColorValue` that other constructors and helpers never produce; keep the unwrapped 360° endpoint separately for ARIA/positioning or normalize the stored color hue.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "new_string": "/// Apply a normalized angle (`0..=1`) to the hue value.\nfn apply_wheel_angle(ctx: &mut Context, angle: f64) {\n    // A full revolution returns to the top, so drags stay in `[0, 360)`.\n    let hue = (angle.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * 360.0) % 360.0;\n\n    set_hue(ctx, hue);\n}\n\n/// Set the hue value (kept unwrapped) and derive the normalized stored color.\n///\n/// [`ColorValue::new`] normalizes the hue into `[0, 360)`, so the stored color\n/// never violates that invariant even when `hue` is the `360°` endpoint.\nfn set_hue(ctx: &mut Context, hue: f64) {\n    ctx.hue_value = hue;\n\n    let color = *ctx.value.get();\n    ctx.value\n        .set(ColorValue::new(hue, color.saturation, color.lightness, color.alpha));\n}"
}

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve alpha when formatting HSB colors**

When a `ColorField` is configured with `color_format: ColorFormat::Hsb` and the current `ColorValue` is translucent (for example from `#3366ff80` or the alpha channel), this formatter emits only hue/saturation/brightness. The field's commit path then reparses that text through `hsb(...)`, which always constructs an opaque color, so simply focusing and blurring the field without edits silently changes alpha to `1.0`. Please make the HSB representation round-trip alpha or avoid committing a lossy formatted value.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F85Qx	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_field/mod.rs:553	dbid=3330488979
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Seed channel-mode value after prop changes**

The earlier spinbutton fix seeds a base color only in `init`; fresh evidence is this `SetProps` path, which can switch an already-mounted empty whole-color field to `channel: Some(...)` without creating a value. In that case the input becomes `role="spinbutton"` but still skips `aria-valuenow/min/max` and keyboard/commit paths no-op because `ctx.value` remains `None`, so dynamic channel-mode changes reintroduce the inaccessible unusable spinbutton state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F85Qz	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_swatch_picker/mod.rs:245	dbid=3330488981
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Let disabled swatch pickers process blur**

If the picker is focused and a parent disables it or replaces `colors` with an empty list, this guard starts dropping the subsequent `Blur` event. The service then remains in `State::Focused` with `focused/focus_visible` still set, so the root continues to expose the focused state even after focus has left; allow `Blur` through while disabled/empty, as the other controls do, so in-flight focus can be cleaned up.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F85Q0	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_slider/mod.rs:713	dbid=3330488984
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use pending color for controlled slider output**

In a controlled `ColorSlider`, drag/key events update `slider_value` and the pending internal color, but `Bindable::get()` still returns the old controlled prop until the parent syncs after `on_change_end`. That makes the same render expose the new position/`aria-valuenow` while computing `aria-valuetext`, thumb background, and hidden input from the old color (e.g. dragging hue from red to blue can announce the blue hue with a red color name); derive the display color from `pending()`/`slider_value` for these attrs, and check the analogous ColorArea path.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F85Q1	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_area/mod.rs:320	dbid=3330488985
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Base controlled area axis updates on pending color**

In controlled `ColorArea`, `get()` continues to return the old prop while keyboard events stage edits internally. If the user changes both axes before the parent round-trips a new prop (for example ArrowRight then ArrowUp), this second axis update is derived from the stale controlled color and overwrites the first pending axis change, while `x_value`/`y_value` still show both moves; use the pending color as the base for axis updates so `on_change_end` and submitted/displayed color do not lose one axis.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========

=== format_color_string ===
pub fn format_color_string(color: &ColorValue, format: ColorFormat) -> String {
    match format {
        ColorFormat::Hex => color.to_hex(color.alpha < 1.0),

        ColorFormat::Rgb => {
            let (red, green, blue) = color.to_rgb();

            if color.alpha < 1.0 {
                format!("rgba({red}, {green}, {blue}, {:.2})", color.alpha)
            } else {
                format!("rgb({red}, {green}, {blue})")
            }
        }

        ColorFormat::Hsl => color.to_css_hsl(),

        ColorFormat::Hsb => {
            let (hue, saturation, brightness) = color.to_hsb();

            format!(
                "hsb({hue:.0}, {:.1}%, {:.1}%)",
                saturation * 100.0,
                brightness * 100.0
            )
        }
    }
}
=== parse dispatch (hsb/hsl/hsba) ===
pub fn parse_color_string(input: &str) -> Option<ColorValue> {
    let trimmed = input.trim();

    if trimmed.starts_with('#') {
        return ColorValue::from_hex(trimmed);
    }

    if let Some(inner) = strip_fn_call(trimmed, "rgba") {
        return parse_rgb_args(inner, true);
    }

    if let Some(inner) = strip_fn_call(trimmed, "rgb") {
        return parse_rgb_args(inner, false);
    }

    if let Some(inner) = strip_fn_call(trimmed, "hsla") {
        return parse_hsl_args(inner, true);
    }

    if let Some(inner) = strip_fn_call(trimmed, "hsl") {
        return parse_hsl_args(inner, false);
    }

    if let Some(inner) = strip_fn_call(trimmed, "hsb") {
        return parse_hsb_args(inner);
    }

    None
}

  "new_string": "/// Parse `h, s%, b%` inside `hsb()` or `h, s%, b%, a` inside `hsba()`.\nfn parse_hsb_args(inner: &str, has_alpha: bool) -> Option<ColorValue> {\n    let parts = inner.split(',').map(str::trim).collect::<Vec<_>>();\n\n    let expected = if has_alpha { 4 } else { 3 };\n\n    if parts.len() != expected {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    let hue = parse_finite_f64(parts[0])?;\n    let saturation = parse_finite_f64(parts[1].strip_suffix('%')?.trim())? / 100.0;\n    let brightness = parse_finite_f64(parts[2].strip_suffix('%')?.trim())? / 100.0;\n\n    let alpha = if has_alpha {\n        parse_finite_f64(parts[3])?\n    } else {\n        1.0\n    };\n\n    // Convert HSB -> HSL: lightness = brightness * (1 - saturation/2).\n    let lightness = brightness * (1.0 - saturation / 2.0);\n\n    let hsl_saturation = if lightness > 0.0 && lightness < 1.0 {\n        (brightness - lightness) / fmin(lightness, 1.0 - lightness)\n    } else {\n        0.0\n    };\n\n    Some(ColorValue::new(\n        hue,\n        hsl_saturation,\n        lightness,\n        alpha.clamp(0.0, 1.0),\n    ))\n}"
}

The thumb position uses the\n        // pending slider_value, so the thumb background and hidden input must\n        // use the pending color too — not the stale controlled red.\n        let mut svc = service(Props {\n            channel: ColorChannel::Hue,\n            value: Some(ColorValue::from_hsl(0.0, 1.0, 0.5)),\n            name: Some(\"hue\".to_string()),\n            ..Props::default()\n        });\n\n        drop(svc.send(Event::DragStart { position: 2.0 / 3.0 })); // hue 240 (blue)\n\n        let api = svc.connect(&|_| {});\n        // value() still reflects the controlled prop (red).\n        assert!((api.value().hue - 0.0).abs() < 1e-9);\n        // The hidden input submits the pending (blue) color, matching the thumb.\n        let hidden = api.hidden_input_attrs();\n        let submitted =\n            ColorValue::from_hex(hidden.get(&HtmlAttr::Value).unwrap()).expect(\"hex\");\n        assert!(\n            (submitted.hue - 240.0).abs() < 1.0,\n            \"hidden input must carry the pending hue, got {}\",\n            submitted.hue\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn hue_max_endpoint_does_not_wrap_to_min() {"

PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F99cL	dbid=3330854111	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_field/mod.rs:1018
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid submitting invalid color fields as empty values**

When a named `ColorField` is invalid, this still emits the hidden input's `name` and only omits the `value` attribute below. A successful hidden input without a value attribute submits an empty string, so a user who types an invalid color after a previous valid value sends `name=` rather than omitting the stale color as the comment/spec intend; guard the name as well, or disable/omit the hidden input while invalid.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F99cM	dbid=3330854112	crates/ars-core/src/color.rs:62
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject non-finite ColorValue components in release**

These finiteness checks disappear in release builds, so programmatic inputs such as `ColorValue::new(f64::NAN, 1.0, 0.5, 1.0)` still construct a value containing NaN/inf and downstream formatting can emit invalid CSS/ARIA like `hsl(NaN, ...)`. The parsers already reject non-finite user input, so the public constructor should enforce the same invariant instead of relying on debug-only assertions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F99cO	dbid=3330854114	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_swatch_picker/mod.rs:null
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Let blur clear a disabled swatch picker**

If the picker is focused and the parent then disables it (or replaces `colors` with an empty list), this guard rejects the subsequent `Blur` event because it only allows prop-sync events through. The service can remain in `State::Focused`, and when the retained `focused_index` is still in range `item_attrs` continues to emit `data-ars-focused` even though the disabled control has lost focus; allow `Blur` through this guard so disabling while focused cannot leave stale focus state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F99cP	dbid=3330854115	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_slider/mod.rs:741
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mirror horizontal slider position in RTL**

For `Props { dir: Direction::Rtl, orientation: Horizontal, .. }`, `on_thumb_keydown` already mirrors ArrowLeft/ArrowRight, but this percentage still maps min to the left and max to the right. That makes RTL keyboard interaction and the rendered thumb/track disagree with the spec's flipped horizontal direction; compute the exposed position from the opposite edge when the horizontal slider is RTL.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F99cQ	dbid=3330854116	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_area/mod.rs:790
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mirror the color-area x axis in RTL**

When `ColorArea` is configured with `dir: Direction::Rtl`, the key handler mirrors the x-axis arrows and the spec says the x gradient flips horizontally, but this custom property always exposes the LTR x percentage. In RTL this leaves the thumb/gradient positions opposite the keyboard semantics (min still appears on the left), so the x percentage should be mirrored before it is emitted.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F-D9B	dbid=3330888050	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/angle_slider/mod.rs:761
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Render the pending angle during controlled interactions**

When `Props::value` is `Some`, drag/key transitions only stage the new angle with `ctx.value.set(...)`, while `Bindable::get()` keeps returning the old controlled prop until the parent sends `SyncValue`. Because the thumb's ARIA values and CSS rotation are rendered through `self.value()` here, a controlled `AngleSlider` does not visually or accessibly move during a drag or keyboard adjustment even though `on_change_end` later reports the pending value; render these attributes from the staged/pending angle instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F-D9D	dbid=3330888053	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_slider/mod.rs:659
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the base color at zero alpha**

For `ColorChannel::Alpha`, starting the gradient with the CSS keyword `transparent` makes the zero-alpha end transparent black, so non-black colors fade through black/gray (for example, a white alpha slider renders black-to-white instead of transparent-white-to-white). Use the same hue/saturation/lightness with alpha 0 for the first stop so the alpha track previews only opacity changes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F-D9E	dbid=3330888054	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_swatch_picker/mod.rs:358
**<sub><sub>![P3 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P3-lightgrey?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp zero grid columns before moving rows**

When a consumer configures `SwatchPickerLayout::Grid` with `columns: 0`, vertical keyboard navigation never moves: `FocusDown` adds zero here, and `FocusUp` subtracts `cols % len`, which is also zero. Since `columns` is a public `usize` prop with no non-zero invariant, clamp it to at least 1 (or reject zero) before using it for row navigation.

  "new_string": "    pub fn new(hue: f64, saturation: f64, lightness: f64, alpha: f64) -> Self {\n        // Coerce non-finite inputs to `0.0` so the type's invariants (finite\n        // components, hue in `[0, 360)`, others in `[0, 1]`) hold in release\n        // builds too — otherwise `NaN`/`inf` would leak into generated CSS and\n        // ARIA. Parsers already reject non-finite user input; this guards the\n        // public constructor against programmatic non-finite values.\n        let finite = |value: f64| if value.is_finite() { value } else { 0.0 };\n\n        Self {\n            hue: CoreFloat::rem_euclid(finite(hue), 360.0),\n            saturation: finite(saturation).clamp(0.0, 1.0),\n            lightness: finite(lightness).clamp(0.0, 1.0),\n            alpha: finite(alpha).clamp(0.0, 1.0),\n        }\n    }"
}

  "new_string": "        // Only submit a value when the field is valid. While invalid, the stored\n        // color is the last *valid* value, which no longer matches the visible\n        // input — submitting it would send a stale color.\n        if let Some(color) = (*self.ctx.value.get()).filter(|_| !self.ctx.invalid) {\n            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Value, color.to_hex(true));\n        }\n\n        // A disabled control is omitted from form submission — and so is an\n        // invalid one, so the field round-trips as absent rather than as an\n        // empty `name=` carrying the stale last-valid color.\n        if self.ctx.disabled || self.ctx.invalid {\n            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Disabled, true);\n        }"

                "hsla({:.0}, {:.1}%, {:.1}%, {:.2})",
                self.hue,
                self.saturation * 100.0,
                self.lightness * 100.0,
                self.alpha,
            )
        } else {
            format!(
                "hsl({:.0}, {:.1}%, {:.1}%)",
                self.hue,
                self.saturation * 100.0,
                self.lightness * 100.0,
            )
        }
    }
```

PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F-MYP	dbid=3330932612	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_slider/mod.rs:240
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Invert pointer positions in RTL sliders**

When a horizontal slider is RTL, `thumb_attrs` renders the minimum value on the right and `on_thumb_keydown` mirrors left/right arrows, but drag start/move still maps a normalized physical position of `0.0` to the minimum. In an RTL horizontal slider, clicking or dragging the left edge therefore sets the minimum even though the minimum thumb position is rendered on the right, so pointer interaction is reversed from the visual and keyboard behavior; invert the normalized position before computing the channel value for RTL horizontal orientation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F-MYQ	dbid=3330932613	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_area/mod.rs:293
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Invert the RTL color-area x coordinate**

For RTL color areas, the thumb renderer flips the x axis so the minimum x-channel value appears on the right and the arrow keys are mirrored, but pointer coordinates still map `x = 0.0` directly to the minimum. In RTL, a user clicking the left side of the area will select the minimum while the component displays that value on the right, making pointer selection disagree with both the visual gradient direction and keyboard behavior; apply the same RTL inversion to the normalized x coordinate before deriving `x_val`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F-MYR	dbid=3330932614	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/angle_slider/mod.rs:443
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accumulate controlled keyboard steps from pending angle**

For a controlled `AngleSlider`, `ctx.value.get()` remains the last parent prop while keyboard adjustments are only staged internally, so holding ArrowRight or pressing it twice before the parent round-trips `SyncValue` recomputes from the stale prop each time and the thumb/hidden input stay stuck at one step. The API comments promise the pending value is rendered during controlled keyboard adjustment, so compute the next keyboard angle from `ctx.value.pending()` (or a separate cached angle) instead of the controlled `get()` value.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F-MYS	dbid=3330932615	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_field/mod.rs:338
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep controlled ColorField output in sync**

When `Props::value` is controlled and the user commits a different whole-color value, this only stages the parsed color internally while `Bindable::get()` (used by `value()`, channel ARIA, and the hidden input) still returns the old prop; at the same time `input_text` is rewritten to the new color. That leaves a controlled field visibly showing the committed color but submitting and exposing the stale parent color, with no callback/effect here for the parent to reconcile it, so either avoid rewriting the displayed text until `SyncValue` or use/report the pending value consistently.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F-MYT	dbid=3330932617	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_swatch_picker/mod.rs:309
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Notify or render controlled swatch selections**

For a controlled `ColorSwatchPicker` (`Props::value = Some(...)`), selecting another item only writes the internal pending value, while selected styling, `api.value()`, and the hidden input all read `ctx.value.get()` and therefore remain on the old controlled prop. Since this machine also emits no selection-change effect/callback, clicks and Space/Enter are effectively inert in controlled mode; either notify the parent of the requested color or render/submit the pending selection consistently.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "new_string": "    #[test]\n    fn rtl_horizontal_inverts_pointer_position() {\n        // In RTL, the physical left edge (position 0.0) is the visual maximum.\n        // Use saturation (0..=1, no hue wrap) so the endpoint reads cleanly.\n        let mut rtl = service(Props {\n            channel: ColorChannel::Saturation,\n            dir: Direction::Rtl,\n            default_value: ColorValue::from_hsl(0.0, 0.0, 0.5),\n            ..Props::default()\n        });\n        drop(rtl.send(Event::DragStart { position: 0.0 }));\n        assert!(\n            (rtl.connect(&|_| {}).value().saturation - 1.0).abs() < 1e-9,\n            \"RTL position 0.0 must select the maximum\"\n        );\n\n        // LTR is unchanged: position 0.0 -> minimum.\n        let mut ltr = service(Props {\n            channel: ColorChannel::Saturation,\n            default_value: ColorValue::from_hsl(0.0, 1.0, 0.5),\n            ..Props::default()\n        });\n        drop(ltr.send(Event::DragStart { position: 0.0 }));\n        assert!((ltr.connect(&|_| {}).value().saturation - 0.0).abs() < 1e-9);\n    }"

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the hue endpoint when syncing controlled values**

When a controlled hue slider moves from any non-red color to the max endpoint, the pending state correctly keeps `slider_value == 360` so `aria-valuenow` can reach `aria-valuemax`; however, once the parent accepts the emitted `ColorValue`, its hue is normalized to `0`, and this sync line re-derives `slider_value` as `0`. That makes the thumb/ARIA jump from the right endpoint back to the minimum even though the user selected the max endpoint. Preserve the cached 360° endpoint when the incoming controlled color matches the pending normalized color (the same pattern should be checked for the hue axis in the other color controls).

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F-UJ3	dbid=3330973090	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_field/mod.rs:1064
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Suppress key shortcuts from composing key events**

When the browser sends a keydown with `KeyboardEventData::is_composing == true` before this context flag has been updated, this handler still dispatches `Enter`/arrow shortcuts, so IME users can accidentally commit a partial color or step a channel while choosing a candidate. Other text inputs in this crate also check the event-level composition flag; include `data.is_composing` here so composing key events are ignored even if the composition lifecycle event has not reached the machine yet.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F-UJ5	dbid=3330973092	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/angle_slider/mod.rs:377
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Normalize angle bounds before clamping**

When consumers provide a custom range with `min > max` or a NaN bound, `f64::clamp` panics at runtime, so dragging or setting an `AngleSlider` with malformed public props can crash the component instead of safely normalizing/rejecting the range. The shared slider code normalizes bounds before clamping; apply the same guard here (and the other direct clamp paths) before using custom `min`/`max`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F-UJ6	dbid=3330973093	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_field/mod.rs:348
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accumulate controlled channel steps from pending value**

In controlled channel mode, repeated Arrow/Page key steps before the parent syncs props keep reading `ctx.value.get()`, which is still the stale controlled value, so two ArrowUp presses from hue 0 both stage hue 1 instead of hue 2. Use the pending value as the base for keyboard channel adjustments so controlled spinbuttons accumulate the same way uncontrolled ones do.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F-UJ7	dbid=3330973094	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_slider/mod.rs:661
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mirror track gradient for RTL horizontal sliders**

For horizontal RTL sliders the input mapping and thumb position put the minimum on the right, but the track gradient is still emitted left-to-right with the minimum color on the left. In RTL this makes the visible color ramp contradict the value selected by dragging/clicking (for example the left edge selects the max hue while showing the min hue), so flip the gradient direction or swap the stops when `dir == Rtl` for horizontal tracks.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "new_string": "/// Wrap a value into the range `[min, max)`.\nfn wrap_value(value: f64, min: f64, max: f64) -> f64 {\n    let range = max - min;\n\n    if !range.is_finite() || range <= 0.0 {\n        return min;\n    }\n\n    (value - min).rem_euclid(range) + min\n}\n\n/// Clamp `value` to `[min, max]` without panicking on malformed bounds.\n///\n/// `min`/`max` are public props with no enforced invariant, so a `min > max`\n/// or non-finite bound would make [`f64::clamp`] panic. In that case the value\n/// is returned unclamped rather than crashing the component.\nfn clamp_to_range(value: f64, min: f64, max: f64) -> f64 {\n    if !min.is_finite() || !max.is_finite() || min > max {\n        return value;\n    }\n\n    value.clamp(min, max)\n}"
}

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp HSB channels before converting**

When a user enters an out-of-range HSB/HSBA value, these parsed percentages are fed into the HSB→HSL math before any clamping happens. For example, `hsb(0, 100%, 200%)` computes lightness as `1.0` and ends up as white, while `hsb(0, 200%, 100%)` ends up as black, instead of clamping the HSB saturation/brightness to `0..=1` and preserving the expected red hue as the color conversion rules require. Clamp `saturation` and `brightness` here before calculating `lightness`/`hsl_saturation`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F-cLE	dbid=3331014873	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_area/mod.rs:750
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Render ColorArea backgrounds from configured axes**

When `ColorArea` is configured with non-default axes such as `x_channel = Hue` or RGB/brightness channels, the value math and thumb ARIA use those axes, but the background still exposes only a fixed hue swatch (`--ars-color-area-bg`). That makes the visible picking surface misleading: dragging across a hue axis changes hue numerically while the background does not show a hue gradient for the user to pick from. Include the configured channels in the generated gradient/data so the background matches the active `x_channel`/`y_channel`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F-cLG	dbid=3331014875	crates/ars-components/src/specialized/color_field/mod.rs:510
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow disabled ColorFields to track descriptions**

When a `ColorField` is disabled, adapter `SetHasDescription(true)` events hit this catch-all and are dropped, so a disabled field that renders helper text never adds the description id to `aria-describedby`. Disabled controls still need their accessible description exposed, and other described input components process this bookkeeping event independent of editability; allow `SetHasDescription` through the inert-state guard.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========

Corners are emitted in visual order (top = the\n        // y-axis maximum since y is inverted; left/right follow the RTL x flip).\n        let (x_min, x_max) = channel_range(self.ctx.x_channel);\n        let (y_min, y_max) = channel_range(self.ctx.y_channel);\n\n        let (left_x, right_x) = if self.ctx.dir == Direction::Rtl {\n            (x_max, x_min)\n        } else {\n            (x_min, x_max)\n        };\n\n        let corner = |x_value: f64, y_value: f64| {\n            let with_x = with_channel(color, self.ctx.x_channel, x_value);\n            with_channel(&with_x, self.ctx.y_channel, y_value).to_css_hsl()\n        };\n\n        attrs\n            .set(\n                HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-x-channel\"),\n                format!(\"{:?}\", self.ctx.x_channel).to_lowercase(),\n            )\n            .set(\n                HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-y-channel\"),\n                format!(\"{:?}\", self.ctx.y_channel).to_lowercase(),\n            )\n            .set_style(\n                CssProperty::Custom(\"ars-color-area-corner-tl\"),\n                corner(left_x, y_max),\n            )\n            .set_style(\n                CssProperty::Custom(\"ars-color-area-corner-tr\"),\n                corner(right_x, y_max),\n            )\n            .set_style(\n                CssProperty::Custom(\"ars-color-area-corner-bl\"),\n                corner(left_x, y_min),\n            )\n            .set_style(\n                CssProperty::Custom(\"ars-color-area-corner-br\"),\n                corner(right_x, y_min),\n            );\n\n        attrs\n    }"

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve parse-invalid state on prop refresh**

When a focused `ColorField` has already failed parsing (for example the user enters `not-a-color` and presses Enter), any later prop refresh that goes through `SetProps` with `props.invalid == false` clears `ctx.invalid` even though `input_text` is still the invalid text. This re-enables the hidden input and removes `aria-invalid`, so a focused field can submit the stale last-valid color while showing an invalid value; keep the parser-derived invalid state separate from the external `invalid` prop or recompute it before clearing.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not clear external invalid state on value sync**

When a controlled `ColorField` has `invalid: true` and the parent updates `value` while keeping `invalid` true (for example, server validation still fails for the new color), `on_props_changed` only enqueues `SyncValue` because the invalid prop itself did not change. This branch then clears `ctx.invalid`, and no following `SetProps` restores it, so the field drops `aria-invalid` and re-enables/submits the hidden input despite the prop still marking it invalid.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
==========
```

The fix: value-setting events (`SyncValue`, `SetValue`) should clear only the parser-derived `parse_error`, never the external `invalid` (owned by the prop / `SetInvalid`).

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Align vertical slider gradients with the vertical axis**

When `orientation` is `Vertical`, this still leaves `to_edge` as `"to right"`, so the emitted track background varies horizontally while the thumb/value move vertically. A vertical color slider therefore shows the same color along its actual travel axis (for hue/alpha/RGB ramps), making clicks/drags visually misleading; choose a vertical direction such as `to top` for vertical orientation.

`ars-components` is compiled as `#![no_std]` when the default `std` feature is disabled, but this new unconditionally-exported module calls std-only `f64` methods such as `atan2`/`to_degrees` here (and similar float helpers like `round` elsewhere in the module). In no-std builds, any consumer that enables `specialized::angle_slider` through the crate will fail to compile; use the same no-std math strategy as the color code or gate the module behind `std`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

This module is also exported in `ars-components` no-std builds, but `f64::rem_euclid` is not available without `std` on this toolchain. The `Increment`/`Decrement` paths therefore make no-default-feature consumers fail to compile once `color_wheel` is added; use a no-std helper (as `ars-core::color` does with `core_maths`) instead of the inherent method.
